profile._sText:
A complete Traditional Chinese (zh-TW, Taiwan) translation of Sonic and the Black Knight (ソニックと暗黒の騎士) for Wii (Japan, RENJ8P), as a Riivolution patch for Dolphin and real Wii consoles.

What's translated

  • All 5,435 lines of text: story cutscene subtitles (31 scenes), in-stage voiced hint subtitles (17 stages), menus, items, weapons, skills, missions, achievements, the Treasury encyclopedia and system messages
  • 50 graphics with Japanese text: the title logo (索尼克與黑暗騎士), menu labels, result and pause screens, the strap warning screens
  • The save data title and comment shown in the Wii menu
  • Names follow SEGA's official Traditional Chinese where it exists (索尼克, 塔爾斯, 納克魯斯, 夏特, 布蕾姿, 希爾弗); the Arthurian cast uses the usual Taiwanese names (亞瑟王, 蘭斯洛特, 高文, 帕西瓦爾, 梅林娜, 卡利巴)

How to install

  1. You need the Japanese Wii disc or image: Sonic to Ankoku no Kishi (Japan), game ID RENJ8P.
  2. Dolphin: copy the riivolution and SonicBK_zhTW folders from the zip into Load\Riivolution\ in Dolphin's user folder, right-click the game → Start with Riivolution Patches, set "Traditional Chinese" to Enabled → Start.
  3. Wii: copy both folders to the root of your SD card and start the game through Riivolution from the Homebrew Channel.
  4. Keep the Wii (or Dolphin's Wii) system language on Japanese.

No game data is included; you need your own copy of the game.
Source code, tools and translation files: GitHub

繁體中文說明

《索尼克與黑暗騎士》Wii 日版（RENJ8P）的台灣繁體中文化，以 Riivolution 補丁發布，Dolphin 與 Wii 實機都能用。劇情字幕、關卡中的提示語音字幕、選單、道具、技能、任務、寶物庫資料與系統訊息共 5,435 句全部中文化，標題 Logo 與選單上的日文圖片也重新繪製。

  1. 準備日版遊戲光碟或映像檔（遊戲代碼 RENJ8P）。
  2. Dolphin：把壓縮檔裡的 riivolution、SonicBK_zhTW 兩個資料夾放進 Dolphin 使用者資料夾的 Load\Riivolution\，對遊戲按右鍵 →「Start with Riivolution Patches」，啟用「Traditional Chinese」後開始。
  3. Wii 實機：兩個資料夾放到 SD 卡根目錄，從 Homebrew Channel 執行 Riivolution。
  4. Wii 主機（或 Dolphin 的 Wii）語言請設為日文。

profile._sText:
Disclaimer: Please do not request other controller options or config tweaks. This is merely just a personal config that we decided to make public for preservation's sake. If you want to make your own edit, please credit me, Vinnygar and LJSTAR. Reasons I did not make this a Dynamic Input pack is because it's not precise with its positioning. I had to manually shift things and sometimes even move words a bit just to make the button spacing consistent. Only the English option is supported. No AI was used in making these assets. 

Controls: 
A Button: X Button 
B Button: Circle Button 
B Button Alternatives: L2 and R2 Triggers 
1 Button: Triangle Button 
2 Button: Triangle Button
- Button: Share and Options (Start and Select)
+ Button: Share and Options (Start and Select) 
Z Button: L1 
Shaking Wiimote: Square Button 
Tilting Wiimote: Right Stick (For reflecting light) 
Final Boss Quickstep: L1 and R1 

Used FOT-Seurat for L1 and R1 to match the original Wii buttons
As a bonus, I changed many basic fonts in the game to FOT-NewCinema to make it more stylistically consistent with Black Knight's graphic design. The Wiimote QTE is replaced with Caliburn for the rival fights.

Put Texture Pack in User\Load\Textures
Put Controller Preset in User\Config\Profiles\Wiimote

profile._sName: Knights of the Round In Any Stage
profile._sText:
Knights of the Round In Any Stage

DETAILS: This mod natively applies Character switching on any stage regardless of Red Colored Icon stages!

WORKS ON REAL HARDWARE!!!!

REQUIREMENTS:
  • Extracted Sonic and the Black Knight Files 
         (Don't know how? Watch This Video!)
  • Unlock The Blacksmith in Adventure Mode!

Made Using:

* ImHex (https://imhex.werwolv.net) 
* Dolphin Memory Engine (https://github.com/dolphin-memory-engine)

INSTALLATION TUTORIAL: 

  • For this, you'll need a hex editor, A WEB VERSION of one would work just fine
  • Locate the "main.dol" file (Usually found in 'Black Knight Game Files\Data\SYS')  Now drag and drop the file onto the hex editor.
  • if you're using the WEB VERSION, Go to the right where you see the "Go To" Text Field, and paste any one of these addresses that corresponds to your Game's Region.

    USA (RENE8P): 0x00130703

    EU (RENP8P): 0x00130723

    JP (RENJ8P): 0x00130773
  •  Example:
  • Press ENTER, It should jump you to a value of "02", change that to "03" and Save it. 
  • OPTIONAL: Alternatively you could just download the RAR, but I Personally wouldn't recommend it, incase I work on other main.dol mods.


KNOWN ISSUES:

  • Their's a bug where sometimes if you complete a Level with Percival, and the Slot resets back to Sonic, upon entering that same stage Sonic's Homing attack velocity would be similar to Percivals.
  • Rival Fights: Clashing USING a character that ISN'T Sonic will CRASH the Game.
  • Dialogue Triggers (HINTS) are mostly broken for the Non Red-Icon stages (Recommend turning hints off in the game's options if that's the case).
  • Wall Maneuver Sections will Freeze a Character that ISN'T Sonic in place.
  • King Arthur Boss fights range from possible, too not possible to beat. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
  • Some missions are simply not possible to do Using the Knights (e.g. Soul surge on ground)

profile._sName: Ai HD Texture Overhaul + Controller Support
profile._sText:
Please Donate to my Kofi for suggestions/support for my future projects! https://ko-fi.com/giodude

This texture pack replaces nearly every texture in the game, each either ai upscaled using ESRGAN and Gigapixel or completely reworked by hand. I've also attached a graphics mod that fixes the low res bloom effect or removes it altogether (turns out the same mod for sonic colors works here). This mod also replaces any Wii remote button prompts with XBOX Series X buttons, as well as coming with a control scheme configuration for dolphin. Here are some of the notable controls below:

A - A
B - B or Right Bumper
1 - Thumb R
2 - Shoulder L
Z - Either Trigger
Tilt Wii remote/use pointer - Right analog stick
Swing sword - X
Shake nunchuck - Y

A Separate download for the original Wii button prompts is also available.

I've also linked a DDS version as I realize that may run much better on low end hardware. The mip-maps are full sized images, making the PNG pack even struggle with 11GB of Vram. I'd recommended the DDS pack in almost all cases, I did not notice a loss of quality.

I'd love feedback if you have any. I can add back in the original Wii controls or make separate control scheme options if there are enough requests. Also please point out of there are any textures that look off or need upscaling so I can add them to the pack.

ESRGAN models used:

4x-AnimeSharp
4x_BSRGAN
8x_NMKD-Typescale_175k

FYI I highly recommend using this with the 60fps patch to make this the smoothest experience possible.

Installation Instructions:

Textures:

  • Download SonicAndTheBlackKnightHD.Zip or SonicAndTheBlackKnightHD_DDS.Zip
  • Extract the RENE8P folder inside and place it in the dolphin custom textures directory. By default this is C:\Users\USERNAME\Documents\Dolphin Emulator\Load\Textures
  • Make sure that "Load Custom Textures" and "Enable Graphics Mods" are enabled in Dolphin's advanced graphics settings. Enable "Prefetch Custom Textures" Only if you have 8gb+ available vram.
     


Xbox Controls:


  • Download xbox_controls.zip
  • Extract the zip file
  • Place SonicBlackKnight.ini in your dolphin wii remote profile directory. By default this is "C:\Users\USERNAME\Documents\Dolphin Emulator\Config\Profiles\Wiimote".
  • If you'd like to have these controls activate on launching the game, right click on the game and go to properties inside of dolphin. Go to the "Editor" tab in game config and paste this at the top of the user config:

    [Controls]

    WiimoteProfile1 = SonicBlackKnight

Original Wii Controls

  • Download "OriginalControls.zip"
  • Inside of the main texture pack there is a folder called "controls". Delete that folder and replace it with the new "controls" folder in the zip file
  • Pair a Wii remote to dolphin


Bloom:

  • Download Bloom.zip
  • Extract the "Sonic and the Black Knight" folder to the Dolphin graphics mods directory. This will be inside wherever you installed dolphin emulator to inside of the "Sys\Load\GraphicMods" directory.
  • Right click on the game and go to properties inside of dolphin. In the graphics mods tab there are 2 options, "Bloom Removal" and "Native Resolution Bloom". Make sure only one of these is ticked. "Bloom Removal" removes bloom while "Native Resolution Bloom" fixes the broken bloom effect at higher resolutions.

60fps:

Here's the Action Replay code for 60fps to save a google search:

040887D8 3800003C

profile._sText:
Ever wanted Sonic and the Black Knight to look more like a modern game? Welp, here you go!


  • FXAA Anti-aliasing - Smooths out the jaggies
  • Screen Space Ambient Occlusion - Adds soft shadows to simulate ambient light
  • Screen Space Global Illumination - Adds some basic lighting
  • Gaussian Animflare - Adds a flare to shiny things
  • Scene Tonemapping - Color correction, making the game look more colorful.
  • Bloom - Adding a subtle glow to bright things
  • Pixel Vibrance - Makes the game more vibrant
  • Depth of Field - Blurs out faraway elements


HOW TO INSTALL

1. Download Ishiiruka Dolphin (Link in requirements)
2. Copy the mod pack and paste the User Folder in the Ishiiruka Dolphin Folder (It should go on top of the existing one, make sure it replaces any files that are there)
3. Add your game file to Ishiiruka Dolphin (just like how you would in regular Dolphin)
4. Play the game!

HOW TO ADD TEXTURE PACK

1. Paste all the textures into [Ishiiruka Dolphin]/User/Load/Textures/RENE8P
2. Make sure that "Load Custom Textures" are enabled in Ishiiruka Dolphin's Advanced Graphics settings.
4. You can enable "Prefetched Textures" if you want a stutter-free experience, but you probably need around 12 GB of RAM at minimum.

This is a mod for Sonic Colors (Wii) that aims to restore the 6 split Acts from the original game, giving a glimpse into how the game potentially played in early development.

It uses the originally intended level structure (2 Acts + Missions), with a separate mod zip that skips the Mission Acts.
The excluded Acts are skipped by spawning Sonic in the goal ring, similar to Colors DX's level order options.

PLEASE REFER TO THE README FILE FOR INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS!

This mod works on all regions of the game, whether it's running on Dolphin or the original Wii hardware (tested by DeaThProj on a Japanese game dump).
However, it hasn't been tested on modded builds like Colors DX, so you're on your own if you want to try that.

It's recommended to play this mod on a completed save file (playing the mod via Egg Shuttle also works).
Make sure to backup your save data before playing!

English:
This mod replaces the English voice acting for the Spanish dub from Sonic Colors Ultimate. However, ve_HNT00_H50_tl_wav is missing and can't be found in SCU's game files. It's a voice line from Tails' hints, so if you decide to turn off those, you won't have a problem.

Installation:

1st method:

- Download the first zip from the alternate download options.
- Use Colors Mod Helper to extract your game's files.
- Copy the "colors_iso_root\files" file from the zip and paste it in the "colors_iso_root" game file.
- Copy the "sonic2010_0\sound" file from the zip and paste it in the "sonic2010_0" game file.
- Repack the game.

2nd method:

- Download the second zip from the alternate download options.
- Extract the xml file in the Riivolution folder inside your Wii's SD card.
- Extract the 'Sonic Colors Spanish Dub' folder inside your Wii's SD card.
- Open Riivolution from your Wii console and apply the patch.

Español:
Este mod reemplaza la actuación de voz inglesa por el doblaje castellano de Sonic Colors Ultimate. Sin embargo, ve_HNT00_H50_tl_wav no está  ya que no se encuentra  en los archivos de SCU. Es una sola línea de voz de las pistas de Tails por lo que, si decides tenerlas desactivadas, no tendrás problemas.

Instalación:

1er método:

- Descarga el primer zip desde las opciones alternativas de descarga.
- Usa Colors Mod Helper para extraer los archivos de tu juego.
- Copia la carpeta "colors_iso_root\files" del zip y pégala en la carpeta "colors_iso_root" del juego.
- Copia la carpeta "sonic2010_0\sound" del zip y pégala en la carpeta "sonic2010_0" del juego.
- Reempaqueta el juego.

2º método:

- Descarga el segundo zip de las opciones alternativas de descarga.
- Extrae el archivo xml en la carpeta de Riivolution de la tarjeta SD de tu Wii.
- Extrae la carpeta 'Sonic Colors Spanish Dub' en la tarjeta SD de tu Wii.

NOTE: REFER TO THE SECOND SCREENSHOT SO THE GAME DOESN'T CRASH!

This ZIP includes the files for Better Sonic for Sonic Colours (Wii)! Here's what we have in-store today!

Better Sonic

Model Changes

- Sonic Generations model

 Material Changes

- Custom fresnel  spheremaps for fur
- Generations shoe reflection
 
- Gens jumpball

 

 Super Sonic

- Same changes applied to Super Sonic

 Installation (PLEASE READ)

EASY WAY: https://github.com/PTKickass/Universal-CPK-Mod-Installer

Already explains how it's used on the repo

YOU WILL NEED TO DOWNLOAD THE TOOLS IN THE LINK BELOW TO INSTALL THE MOD FILES. SkythTools download:
- https://github.com/blueskythlikesclouds/SkythTools/archive/refs/heads/master.zip 

Installation guide 
-----------------------------

First you'll need to dump your copy of Sonic Colors/Colours with Dolphin. 

1) Right click the game and select the "Properties" button. Look at the top right of the newly opened properties window and select the "Filesystem" tab. Here you will see the disc partitions and other game related files. 

2) Select "Disc" at the top and right click it. Then select the "Extract Entire Disc..." option. Make a folder in a safe place and name it "Sonic Colors" then extract the disc to that folder. 

3) Wait for the files to fully extract and then go into that folder. You should see a "DATA" folder open it and navigate to the "files" folder and open it as well. You should see a file named "Sonic2010_0.cpk". 

4) Click and drag the "Sonic2010_0.cpk" file into PackCPK (Provided in the link of SkythTools above and located in the "Common" folder) 

5) Wait for the file to fully extract and create a folder named "Sonic2010_0" then open it. 

6) Copy the contents of the mod folder's "Sonic2010_0" folder into yours and accept the file replacement popup. 

7) Wait for the files to transfer and then go back into the "files" folder of your extracted copy of Colors. 

8) Now, select YOUR "Sonic2010_0" folder and click and drag it into PackCPK. Then wait for the tool to repack the cpk file. 

9) Once that is finished you need to delete YOUR "Sonic2010_0" FOLDER. Once that it deleted switch back to the dolphin emulator. 

10) Navigate to the top left of the Dolphin window and select the "Open" button that looks like a disc in a folder. 

11) Naviagate to the directory of your extracted copy of Sonic Colors. 

12) Go into the "DATA" folder once again, then this time open the "sys" folder. Select the "main.dol" file and click open. 

13) Let the game boot up and Enjoy playing the mod! 

Hope y'all like this!

profile._sText:
Sonic Colors HD/DX is a bundle of original modifications to the original (wii) Sonic Colors on a modified version of the Dolphin Emulator, with the goal of bringing the game up to modern graphics standards.

This mod aims to be more faithful to the original design than Sonic Colors: Ultimate, while containing fewer glitches.

The mod is bundled with everything you need to play EXCEPT for a copy of the game. That would be piracy.
Please obtain a rip of Sonic Colors in .wbfs or .iso form yourself.
.nkit.iso IS NOT COMPATIBLE!!!!
Google is your friend here ;)


Features:

  • Easy One-Click install script
  • Preconfigured for 16:9, FHD to 4kHD, 60fps, Fast Loading, Unleashed/Gens control map
  • Original, high-poly Sonic model with improved shading
  • Original, high-poly model for most stage objects (rings, wisp capsules, springs, etc)
  • Fixed and improved bloom (Original bloom removed from stages and replaced with a post process shader)
  • Improved unleashed-inspired color grading
  • Improved lighting (SSAO on Normal, SSGI+SSAO on High & stage specific tweaks)
  • HD UI textures (thanks to triforce141 for letting me use his upscales!)
  • HD textures for objects and enemies (some by triforce141, some original)
  • 60fps fix for Aquarium Park Act 1
  • Depth of Field Effect (Normal Graphics and above)
  • Restored stages to originally intended order (Optional, see Configure script)


Installation:

Install script (Recommended, Windows Only)

  1. Run "StartSonicColors.bat" Installation will happen automatically.


Manual install (aka: what the install script does for you)

Replace with the path to the extracted mod files.
  1. Download Ishiiruka-Dolphin (not normal dolphin!) for your platform, and place it in /Resources/Ishiiruka-Dolphin (Do not override "User")
  2. Copy the contents of /Resources/modules to and overwrite all. Do the same with any modules you with to install.
  3. Extract sonic colors using dolphin, to /Extract game to this folder
  4. Using a sonic-compatible cpk unpacker (such as skythtools), unpack /Extract game to this folder/DATA/files/sonic2010_0.cpk
  5. Copy the contents of /modded files to your newly extracted Sonic_2010 folder, overwriting all.
  6. Repack Sonic2010.cpk and overwrite the original
  7. Run the dolphin executable for your platform from /Resources/Ishiiruka-Dolphin and enjoy!


Known Issues:

  • Loading screens may freeze for 1-2 seconds before starting the level
  • (Emulation issue) Very rarely, some objects may flicker to a solid color for a single frame
  • (60fps issue) you need to boost to clear a certain ramp in Asteroid Coaster Act 4
  • (60fps issue) In the "Targets" mission of Tropical Resort, you will be incorrectly redirected if targeting a certain laser crystal (Fix: Target any other crystal)
  • (60fps issue) In Tropical Resort Act 1, you can get stuck between a few sets of springs if running into them without ever moving horizontally. (Fix: Restart from pause menu and homing attack the springs)

profile._sText:
This mod retextures Sonic's model to specific skins that were added as customization options in Sonic Colors Ultimate.

A new bundle is available for these skins, that allows for easier implementation with Dolphin's custom textures feature.

The skins that have been backported are the following...

  1. Paint Splatter Skins
  2. Tie-Dye Skins
  3. Cheetah Skins
  4. Tiger Skins
  5. Zebra Skins
  6. Zigzag Skins
  7. Galactic Skins
  8. Grid Pattern Skins
  9. Dotted Pattern Skins

Each of the retexture packs has been uploaded separately.
However, there is a bundle that contains all of these skins in a smaller texture size. It is recommended that you use this bundle if you're modding the game on original hardware, as the original Wii textures were 128x128 pixels wide, and the textures from SCU double in size, which might exceed memory limitations and cause crashes.

While simple color swaps for shoes and gloves aren't included, the more complex skin patterns are featured in this mod.

To install this mod, follow the instructions below...

  1. You will have to dump your copy of Sonic Colors with Dolphin, for this, right-click the game from the emulator and select the "Properties" button. From there select the "Filesystem" tab. You'll see the disc partitions and some of the game's files. Select "Disc" at the top and right-click it. Then select the "Extract Entire Disc..." option. 
  2. Make a folder in a safe place and name it "Sonic Colors" then extract the disc to that folder. Wait for the files to extract and then go into that folder. You should see a "DATA" folder, open it and navigate to the "files" folder and open it as well. You should see a file named "Sonic2010_0.cpk".
  3. Now you have to dump the game's Sonic2010_0.cpk, I'd recommend you make a backup of this file at this point since you'll mostly be editing its contents when you apply mods.
  4. Once you're done making your backups you have to dump Sonic2010_0.cpk, I personally used Cri Packed File Maker to unpack it, but there are other tools that can unpack/repack CPK files. If you want to use this tool, however, you can download it from here. Extract crifilesystem.rar and open CriPackedFileMaker.exe.
  5. Once you start this program, you will see two diamond-shaped buttons on the top right corner, click on the one that is not grayed out to select the CPK file you want to unpack (Sonic2010_0.cpk). After doing this you will notice that the other diamond-shaped button that was grayed out before, is now in color. When you click on this second button you will see a window where you have to select the output directory for your CPKs files. Make a folder (preferably on your desktop) and name it "Sonic2010_0" then select this folder as the directory that you want to extract the CPKs files to.
  6. Once the files are done extracting, you can copy the mod's files into the "Sonic2010_0" folder that you created and then proceed to repack your CPK. 
  7. For repacking, go back to Cri Packed File Maker and click on the folder icon at the top part. Then you'll have to select the "Sonic2010_0" folder that contains your modded files, after that, click on the "Build CPK File" button, on the bottom right corner. From there, you will have to set the directory where you want your new Sonic2010_0.cpk to be in.
  8. After the tool is done repacking your CPK file, navigate to where the NEW Sonic2010_0.cpk file is and copy it to where the original Sonic2010_0.cpk was in your game's files, that being the "DATA\files" directory.
  9. Once you're done copying your new CPK into your game's files, open Dolphin again and navigate to the top left of the window, select the "Open" button that looks like a disc in a folder. Navigate to the directory of your extracted copy of Sonic Colors, go into the "DATA" folder once again, then this time open the "sys" folder. Select the "main.dol" file and click open. Once you do this, Dolphin will boot up your game with your modded files.

If you are using dolphin you can actually run the game from an unpacked ISO, as long as you dump your copy of the game by selecting the "Extract Entire Disc..." option from the properties/filesystem tab in dolphin.

profile._sText:
With the release of Sonic Colours Ultimate we've gotten our hands on some really interesting files from the original game, including test levels. With the use of some tools we are able to backport these levels to the original Wii release of Sonic Colours. The levels come from the original, as in the file system of the 2021 re-release of the game they can be found in the "sonic2010" folder. Everything in that folder has originally came from Sonic Team while developing Sonic Colours, but Blind Squirrel Entertainment has made some changes to the files in there, like adding the Jade Wisp Anchors to the set data of the stages. This is super interesting since this is the first time ever we've seen test levels for a boost game.

stg901 - Object Test Map

This test level is used to test various objects and their functions in the game. In the Ultimate version of the level a 100 ring (SuperRingSuper) is present behind the wisp capsules, but due to it not existing in the Wii version of the game it's not here in this port. It was very likely an object added to the level by Blind Squirrel Entertainment.

stg902 - Nishimura Test Map

This test level is used to test the drill wisp's functionality, the drifting mechanism, interactions with slopes, boxes and sky diving.

stg905 - Multi Object Test Map

This test level is used to test various multiplayer objects.

stg904 - Enemy Test Map

This test level is used to test various enemies such as the Chaser, Motora and Big Chaser.

stg906 - Sugawara Test Map

This test level is a variation of stg902 | Nishimura Test Map. From the naming of the maps it seems like at least two developers were using this map as a test level while doing development.

Changes from stg902:

- The "Ring" object is removed.
- There are 3 more "SuperRing" objects.
- Removes the 4 "CommonFloor" objects.
- The "PhantomCancelCollision" has been removed.

In the Ultimate version of the level a Park Token (Token) is present behind the next to the 10 Rings but due to it not existing in the Wii version of the game it's not here in this port. It was very likely an object added to the level by Blind Squirrel Entertainment.

stg999 - For confirmation test

This test level is likely used as a load test.

THE FOLLOWING LEVELS HAVE BEEN REPLACED:

Tropical Resort: Act 1 - stg901
Tropical Resort: Act 2 - stg902
Tropical Resort: Act 3 - stg905
Tropical Resort: Act 4 - stg904
Tropical Resort: Act 5 - stg906
Tropical Resort: Act 6 - stg999

THE TEST LEVELS REPLACE LEVELS IN TROPICAL RESORT, THUS A SAVE FILE THAT HAS THE LEVELS UNLOCKED IN TROPICAL RESORT IS REQUIRED TO USE THIS MOD.

KNOWN ISSUES

- stg901 gives a few issues while ran in Dolphin, pressing OK on these will make the game pass just fine and the level will load.

THE MOD HAS NOT BEEN TESTED ON A REAL HARDWARE AND I DO NOT TAKE ANY RESPONSIBILITY FOR ISSUES THAT OCCUR ON REAL HARDWARE. USE AT YOUR OWN RISK.

INSTALLATION PROCESS:

  1. Make a copy of your Sonic Colors ISO, to avoid modifying the original.
  2. Extract the ISO files in Dolphin. (Right Click Game -> Properties -> Filesystem -> Right Click Disc -> Extract Entire Game)
  3. Download PackCPK.
  4. Extract the contents of "sonic2010_0.cpk" with PackCPK.
  5. Place the files from the mod's "sonic2010_0" folder into the extracted "sonic2010_0" folder.
  6. Drag the extracted folder on PackCPK to repack the files.
  7. Download & Open WiiScrubber.
  8. Click on "Load ISO," and select your copy of Sonic Colours.
  9. Click the + symbol next to Partition:1
  10. Right-click on the file at the bottom of the list, "sonic2010_0.cpk," and select "replace."
  11. Select the newly created cpk from PackCPK's output.
  12. Make sure you close WiiScrubber once it finishes replacing the file.

Hello there!

This is something iulian created in a few minutes (ended up taking 3-4 days) and wanted me to upload. We ended up going in circles with the model stuff due to issues, but finally got there, and I setup the CSB stuff. Thank you, Goldy, for allowing us to use your Jason voices! I guess this is also a sneak peak to Redux Sonic v3 or Gens, as we're using the same mats here, but specifically for Colours (falloff is a combination of the spec and fal map).

NOTE: REFER TO THE SECOND SCREENSHOT SO THE GAME DOESN'T CRASH!

This ZIP includes the files for Redux Sonic for Sonic Colours (Wii)! Here's what we have in-store today!

Redux Sonic (Marza inspired)

Model Changes

- Sonic Colours cutscene model
- Unleashed model arms, mouth, eyes, nose and shoes

Material Changes

- Custom fresnel (reflection) spheremaps for fur
- Unleashed shoe and eye cubemaps as spheremaps
 (iulian set these matcaps up in Gens with a custom stage, I took the photo and then edited it in Photoshop. iulian made further fixes and the other refs. These mats are also used for the new MSA2 v6 models!)
- SU/Gens jumpball texture

Sound Changes & Fixes

- Fixed sound effects for Sonic (volume and pitch adjustments)
- Higher quality jump, spin, boost, stomp, water running (water slider) and homing attack sounds from Unleashed
- Footsteps are no longer weirdly quiet
- Other sound balancing
- Added some oomph factor to the stomp land sound
- Enemy explosions and damage are no longer super quiet
- Gens 1up jingle and fixed the issue where this sound is playing more on the Left audio channel
- Common object sound mixing is much better too
- Jason-senpai's lovely voice (thanks Goldy!)

Super Sonic

- Same changes applied to Super Sonic, but he does not have any model updates.
- Worldmap assets use the OG models and lower res textures for optimisation

Installation (PLEASE READ)


YOU WILL NEED TO DOWNLOAD THE TOOLS IN THE LINK BELOW TO INSTALL THE MOD FILES. SkythTools download:
- https://github.com/blueskythlikesclouds/SkythTools/archive/refs/heads/master.zip 

Installation guide 
-----------------------------

First you'll need to dump your copy of Sonic Colors/Colours with Dolphin. 

1) Right click the game and select the "Properties" button. Look at the top right of the newly opened properties window and select the "Filesystem" tab. Here you will see the disc partitions and other game related files. 

2) Select "Disc" at the top and right click it. Then select the "Extract Entire Disc..." option. Make a folder in a safe place and name it "Sonic Colors" then extract the disc to that folder. 

3) Wait for the files to fully extract and then go into that folder. You should see a "DATA" folder open it and navigate to the "files" folder and open it as well. You should see a file named "Sonic2010_0.cpk". 

4) Click and drag the "Sonic2010_0.cpk" file into PackCPK (Provided in the link of SkythTools above and located in the "Common" folder) 

5) Wait for the file to fully extract and create a folder named "Sonic2010_0" then open it. 

6) Copy the contents of the mod folder's "Sonic2010_0" folder into yours and accept the file replacement popup. 

7) Wait for the files to transfer and then go back into the "files" folder of your extracted copy of Colors. 

8) Now, select YOUR "Sonic2010_0" folder and click and drag it into PackCPK. Then wait for the tool to repack the cpk file. 

9) Once that is finished you need to delete YOUR "Sonic2010_0" FOLDER. Once that it deleted switch back to the dolphin emulator. 

10) Navigate to the top left of the Dolphin window and select the "Open" button that looks like a disc in a folder. 

11) Naviagate to the directory of your extracted copy of Sonic Colors. 

12) Go into the "DATA" folder once again, then this time open the "sys" folder. Select the "main.dol" file and click open. 

13) Let the game boot up and Enjoy playing the mod!

Generations Mods


If you haven't seen these mods for Generations, here are the links to those!

Download Pure SU Sonic here!

Download Marza Sonic here!

Final words

This mod was made in 4 days and might have an oversight (I'm unsure tbh but it seems perfectly fine lol), as we're pretty busy and managed to make this. If you have any feedback to provide, please feel free to drop us a tweet @GensRedux, or comment on this page!

Hope you lot like this!

Better Super Mario Sunshine Online (BSMSO) brings real online multiplayer to Super Mario Sunshine. Each player runs their own Dolphin instance, and a separate easy to use launcher program that has everything you will need to run this mod!

What to expect

  • Up to 10 players in one session
  • You'll be able to see other players movement and animations being synced, FLUDD spraying,  Yoshi, Yoshi spraying spray, and nametags
  • Implemented Custom Model support, currently have 15 models to choose from, with some having custom animations!
Co-op progression

  • Collectables, such as shines and blue coins are synced properly and you can complete a full 120 shine run 
  • All story and plaza states are sync
  • Red coin and related mission progress kept in sync across the lobby, can tag team red coins if in the same episode
  • If anyone joins in the middle of a run, their counters will match the current state of the games progress
  • Option to disable flag syncing to do online races instead of coop
Launcher/Hosting

  • Launcher program to host or join servers — easily setup everything needed within the launcher
  • Host can warp players to stages; clients can warp themselves when enabled
  • Connected Players roster so you can see who’s online and where they are in the game, as well as real time changes when going to different levels
  • Update module within the launcher when a new release occurs / launcher update checks so everyone stays on a compatible build
Game modes

  • Normal co-op for playing through the game together
  • Hide & Seek with host-assigned or pick random seekers, a timed hide grace period, and random level picker
Requirements

profile._sText:
WHEN YOU OPEN TEXTURE PACK PLACE THE GMS FILE INTO THE LOAD => TEXTURE (DO NOT PLACE THE FULL TEXTURE PACK INTO IT, TEXTURES WILL NOT POP UP) 

PACK YOUR SUNGLASSES — ISLE DELFINO IS GETTING A LITTLE EXTRA SUNSHINE!

Welcome to Sunshine Reimagined, a colorful texture makeover for Super Mario Sunshine on Dolphin!

This passion project brings a little more warmth, character, and tropical fun to your next vacation with Mario and FLUDD. The idea is to refresh the artwork while keeping that cheerful, slightly cartoony Sunshine feeling we love.

Expect colorful island scenery, a crayon-style holiday map, a shiny candy-slime LIFE meter, and goop that looks sticky enough to give FLUDD a very busy afternoon!

WHAT’S INSIDE?

• Refreshed environment textures, including grass, sand and dirt transitions, stonework, thatched roofs, and other island surfaces.

• Colorful crayon-style map artwork with playful icons and a warm beige-paper background.

• A coordinated candy-slime LIFE meter, including all 19 component textures, refreshed LIFE lettering, and recognizable filled and depleted pieces.

• An updated Mario life-counter portrait to give the HUD a little extra personality.

• Glossy goop and portal artwork, including rainbow slime and dark, sticky liquorice-style candy goop.

• A standalone collection of 2,399 texture files. No separate base texture pack is required!

HIGH-RESOLUTION, SUNSHINE-STYLE

The artwork is designed for crisp, colorful 4K gameplay while keeping Super Mario Sunshine recognizable.

Texture dimensions vary to suit each asset. “For 4K gameplay” does not mean that every texture is a native 4096 × 4096 image.

This is a visual texture makeover, not a new campaign or gameplay overhaul. No game copy, emulator, or new levels are included.

HOW TO INSTALL

1. Close Dolphin. Back up your existing Sunshine texture installation and disable other Sunshine texture packs to avoid conflicting files.

2. Place the downloaded ZIP, still zipped, in the ResourcePacks directory inside your Dolphin user folder.

3. Open Dolphin’s Resource Pack Manager and install/activate OrlandoUltraTextures. This is the current internal pack name.

4. Enable Load Custom Textures in Dolphin’s Graphics settings.

5. Start Super Mario Sunshine and enjoy your refreshed island vacation!

MANUAL INSTALLATION ALTERNATIVE

With Dolphin closed, extract only the ZIP’s textures/GMS folder into your Dolphin user folder’s Load/Textures directory.

The result should be Load/Textures/GMS, not Load/Textures/GMS/GMS.

Use either manual installation or Resource Pack Manager, not both. Full instructions are included in README.txt.

DOWNLOAD AND REQUIREMENTS

• Game: Super Mario Sunshine — GameCube version.

• Emulator: Dolphin.

• Download size: approximately 5.76 GB.

• Installed texture size: approximately 16.5 GB.

• Allow at least 17 GB free in addition to the downloaded ZIP and any backup you keep.

• You will need your own game copy.

Compatibility with other major mods, other ports, and original hardware has not been verified.

RELEASE-CANDIDATE NOTES

This download is version 1.0.0-rc2.

The texture files and archive have passed technical structure and integrity checks. However, the exact packaged release has not undergone a complete fresh gameplay playthrough, and the newest dark candy goop still needs its final in-game appearance check.

This download contains textures only. Four scene-specific texture-ID improvements for Airstrip, Bianco, Noki, and Ricco depend on separate development scene patches that are not included. Those particular changes will not automatically appear from this texture ZIP alone.

SPOTTED SOMETHING THAT NEEDS A LITTLE MORE SUNSHINE?

Feedback is welcome!

If you notice a texture issue, please include:

• The level and location.

• A screenshot of the issue.

• Your Dolphin version.

• Whether another texture pack or mod is enabled.

These details make it much easier to find the right texture and improve the pack.

Grab FLUDD, soak up the color, and enjoy a fresh trip around Isle Delfino!

Sunshine Reimagined Texture Pack

By OrlandoUltraTextures

An unofficial fan texture pack. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo.

Changelog can be found here: https://pastebin.com/gQSN3VGd
If you require any previous version please contact me on discord (@warspyking)


I highly recommend watching the trailer for a more comprehensive idea of what this hack is.

This is, a work in progress of 3 months. Which is a lot, y'know. I never intended for it to take that long, it started as a fun "yeah I'll make something for a few weeks for dootmeisterr to play when he gets his pc repaired" but it became more and more apparent that it was going to take... much longer than that. If you had told me it would take 3 months when I started I probably would have been too overwhelmed to start, but I'm so thankful I didn't realize that myself because I am very happy I made this.

I want to talk a bit about what this hack actually IS. Because I don't think that's super clear, I did my best to communicate it in the video but I want to be more straightforward in text. The best way to talk about what this hack is, is to first talk about what it isn't. This hack is NOT a super polished super fair modern day kaizo that you'd find in like mario maker or on smwcentral or anything like that. It's also not exactly a collection of remixes per se, either, because it does have some pretty nonstandard stuff at times. The hack is, in it's nature, pretty messy, and I want to be clear that I do not view that as a fault, it was actually a guiding principle. Please, do not underestimate this hack. Even if it is not something that appeals to you.

This hack is meant to be rough around the edges, and it's meant to prioritize quantity over quality (to an extent). It's not meant to have a difficulty curve and it's not meant to be fair. That's not to say it isn't fun or fair, but moreso that this hack really harkens back to kaizo origin. Making something to bully your good friends with. Most of the time that comes from difficulty, but there are hints of humor and frustration in there too y'know. This hack is simply about me taking SMS and making something wacky, evil, cruel, or just fun out of every single shine and blue coin. What that actually entails, well, you'll just have to find out.

Which is why, once you advance the plaza state, the game completely opens up to you. I recognize many people that will want to play this aren't necessarily sunshine gods, and I know there ARE parts of the game that many people could enjoy (especially with savestates! Highly recommend!), that they would otherwise be locked out of. So, shine requirements for progression/episode selection have been completely removed. I know this kinda kills any%, but I'm not convinced people were going to run this game or work towards a greater goal to begin with. If that is a legitimate interest, please do play for 45 shines or something! I encourage it completely!

Insert some mushy story about my good friend dootmeisterr who this hack is clearly dedicated to.

Please enjoy. Thank you.

profile._sText:
• This is a pack of alphabet textures for the purpose of editing the "SHINE!" animation, as well as "TOO BAD!", "READY", and "GO!".
  • The game originally only had a limited set of characters, because not every letter in the alphabet was used.
  • The textures go as follows: A, B, D, E, G, H, I, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, U, Y, and an exclamation point.
  • This pack adds C, F, J, K, L, Q, V, X, Z, and a blank space character.
  • Here's how it works.
  • The alphabet texture set in the original game is located in data/game_6.szs, inside of the 'timg' folder.
  • The actual animation file for controlling what letters the animation displays is in the 'scrn' folder, named 'big_tx_1.blo'.
  • Normally, I would use a tool like blojob to edit this file, but that tool does not detect dependencies correctly, so the textures won't load.
  • So, I've been doing it manually with a hex editor. Personally, I use HxD.

Here are the offsets for big_tx_1.blo:

GO!:
0x6F-0x0A - big_tx_g.bti
0xB7-0xC2 - big_tx_o.bti
0xFF-0x10A - big_tx_ex.bti

SHINE!:
0x14B-0x156 - big_tx_s.bti
0x193-0x19D - big_tx_h.bti
0x1DA-0x1E6 - big_tx_i.bti
0x223-0x22E - big_tx_n.bti
0x26B-0x276 - big_tx_e.bti
0x2B3-0x2BF - big_tx_ex.bti

TOO BAD!:
0x2FF-0x30A - big_tx_t.bti
0x347-0x352 - big_tx_o.bti
0x38F-0x39A - big_tx_o.bti
0x3D7-0x3E2 - big_tx_b.bti
0x41F-0x42A - big_tx_a.bti
0x467-0x472 - big_tx_d.bti
0x4AF-0x4BB - big_tx_ex.bti

READY:
0x4FB-0x506 - big_tx_r.bti
0x543-0x54E - big_tx_e.bti
0x58B-0x596 - big_tx_a.bti
0x5D3-0x5DE - big_tx_d.bti
0x61B-0x626 - big_tx_y.bti

  • You can change what the animation says by changing the letter in big_tx_*.bti in a hex editor.
  • In the hex editor, you can't change the file size without the game crashing.
  • If you want to replace an exclamation point with a letter, you have to copy and rename whichever letter you want to have one extra character for padding.
  • What I usually do is copy the letter texture and add a character. For example, big_tx_dd.bti.

  • Super Mario Sunshine's ARAM is already tightly packed, so be sure only to copy textures you need and delete extra textures you don't need.
  • If you put too many textures into game_6, it takes up too much memory, and the the game spits out some hilariously broken results.
  • Adding all of the textures from this pack will not make the game crash on its own. I have tested it many times. It only started becoming unstable when I added like 20 more textures into it.

Calling all Count Bleck fans! 


I’m about to make your dream (and mine) come true.  What if Count Bleck was both the hero and the villain of the story? Well, it's now possible in Super Paper Bleck! This mod comes with a fully playable Count Bleck with almost every Mario's animations replaced by the ones that fit best. 

This mod is compatible with every region of the game, thanks to Dunkaccina who helped me figure out why it didn't and works on both Dolphin and hardware.

 This is my first mod so I hope I didn't make any(more) mistake. 

How to install :


For Dolphin:

1- Extract the ZIP and move the "Super Paper Bleck" folder to Documents/Dolphin Emulator/Load/Riivolution

2- Move the "Super Paper Bleck.xml" Riivolution XML file to Documents/Dolphin Emulator/Load/Riivolution/riivolution

3- Launch Dolphin, right click on your SPM game and click on "Start with Riivolution Patches…"

4- If you have correctly placed the XML it should already be there and all you have to do is to enable it. If it isn't there, you can always open it with "Open Riivolution XML…"

For console:

1- Extract the ZIP and move the "Super Paper Bleck" folder to the root of your SD card.

2- Move the "Super Paper Bleck.xml" Riivolution XML file to the riivolution folder in the root of your SD card.

3- Launch Riivolution, enable the mod and select launch.

Have fun! BLEH HEH HEH HEH! BLECK!

profile._sText:
(This is a demo of Partially Realio, not the full game. Read below for more information.)

Partially Realio is a postmodern neo-repaint of Super Paper Mario. Despite having the same framework, it is an entirely new story, with new characters and worlds inspired by classic comedy novels such as Discworld and Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Play as Realio, a mysterious mute bastardization of Mario as him and his team travel through Wizardtopia, a vast land fueled by the mind and our imagination. The focus on comedic worldbuilding is sure to keep you laughing the entire game, but the heavy story will keep you at the edge of your seat.

You do not need to have played Super Paper Mario beforehand, as the game will explain every mechanic to you as if you've never played it before. All you need is a basic understanding of the great Mario, and you will be able to enjoy this story.

Content Warning:
Partially Realio contains dark themes of abuse, with allusions, but not outright showcases, of bigotry. There is also a character who uses a slur they cannot reclaim, but is specifically called out for this behavior. There is a decent amount, but not majority, of crass, lowbrow humor in the mod, but this is extremely intentional. I hope you understand why.

NOTE FOR STREAMERS: Partially Realio contains copyrighted music. None of the songs used should get you taken down, but VODs will almost certainly be demonetized. I'm sorry for the inconvenience (trust me, I'm a YouTuber, I get it) but the truth is that Realio wouldn't be good enough to play or watch without its music choices, in my eyes. I don't want to sacrifice my art. I hope you understand.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • What does this mod change?
Currently only textures, audio and text. Future versions might include gameplay changes, but that would only be if a modder able to do so was willing to work with me. (Please contact me if you're able and willing.) For now, this is merely a story mod.

  • What is a repaint, and how is Realio a neo-repaint?
A repaint is a form of shitpost mod where textures are replaced with random images, usually contemporary memes, for the purpose of comedy, popularized by the group Games Repainted. Realio is a "neo-repaint"  because it takes this anarchic artform and attempts to tell a narrative within the restrictions of a repaint.

  • How do I play this mod?
Instructions are included in the mod itself. All you need is a ROM of Super Paper Mario and Dolphin.

  • Can I play this mod on console?
Future versions are planned to include console compatibility, but for now, Realio is too dependent on Dolphin's custom texture feature. If it helps, you can still play the game with a Wiimote, and basically any computer from the last 10 years can run Dolphin.

  • How is this a "demo" build? How much is finished?
The entire main story is playable from start to finish (including some postgame content) with every line of dialogue changed. Some optional dialogue is already done, but not all of it. Textures are also very unfinished, but there's enough for you to immerse yourself in Realio's atmosphere. In short, this is far from the complete mod, but you still have a full 13-15 hour RPG's worth of story to chew on.

  • Why are you releasing a demo? It's clearly unfinished.
To put it simply, while I love this mod and everything in it, I've been working on it for over 2 years now, and I am undergoing a bit of burnout. If I forced myself to make the mod completely finished before release, it would likely cause the project to be cancelled, and even if I stuck through, it would take at least an extra year just to do so, and to be blunt, it wouldn't be as good. I have many other large projects I want to do that have been put aside because of Realio, so instead of continuing to do that, I get to release Realio in a state I'm comfortable with and take a break to create even more weird projects that you're sure to enjoy. In short, you get more projects from me, I get to have more creative freedom, and Realio will overall be a better and more enjoyable experience when it's finished. And even if it never gets finished, you still have this. We both win.

  • This mod is pretentious and stupid.
Ultimately, I made this mod for myself, and my sense of humor is very specific. There is an audience that will be turned off by jokes about philosophy and psychology, but even ignoring the fact that most of the humor in the mod is pretty easy to comprehend, I know that as long as I exist, and it's something I will enjoy, then there is another person that will. I think we focus too much on things that make sense, and often fetishize the norm, pushing this asinine idea that a piece of art indistinguishable from reality makes it superior, ESPECIALLY video games, when art is good because it provides a biased fun-house mirror look at reality. Realio isn't trying to be smart. Well, it is, but it isn't trying to prove that I'm smarter than you. It's a showcase that you can be dumb and smart at the same time, and how both compliment the other, and that any form of art is as valid as any other form. Intelligence as we know it is malleable as clay, and like a stat point in an RPG, can be applied in many different ways depending on what you want to specialize in. So, to answer your non-question: A little bit, but I tried my best to know who I am and know my limits.

Hold LB to centre and show the pointer. Move the right stick to tilt in each direction. Use RB to select.

Setup:

  • Download R8PX01.ini
  • Open Dolphin and go to File > Open User Folder then follow these steps to get to the right folder.
Windows/Mac

Go to Config > Profiles > Wiimote

Steam Deck/Linux

Go up in the directory until you see a config folder

Then go to config > dolphin-emu > Profile > Wiimote
On Steam Deck flatpak it looks like this:

/home/deck/.var/app/org.DolphinEmu.dolphin-emu/config/dolphin-emu/Profiles/Wiimote

Continued

  • Move the R8PX01.ini file into this folder
  • Confirm this is correct by going to Options > Controller Settings > Wii Remote 1 Configure. Check that R8PX01 is available from the dropdown. You can also change some mappings from here. Press Load, make your edits, then be sure to Save.
  • You may need to change which device is connected. In this case you may have to also update the inputs. If you follow the maps above you should have the same setup with your connected controller. To set up the hidden pointer, go to Motion Simulation > Hide and add an exclamation point before the input ("!TL")

Hi! Thanks for checking out the Play as Ghirahim mod!

This is a mod that's created for use with the Skyward Sword Randomizer. It is however compatible with the non randomized version of the game as well, just less so, since the cutscenes will not be edited.

Please note that at this time, only the model itself can be used with the HD version.

So, assuming you’re using one of the newer versions of the randomizer, there should be a folder named “models” in your randomizer folder, right next to your randomizer exe. You can just take the three folders named “Ghirahim”, “Ghirahim 2nd form” and “Ghirahim Final Form” and plop them down in the models folder. After that, you will be able to select the three different forms of Ghirahim within the randomizer program.

If you just want to use the player models without using the custom item models, custom text, custom icons, etc you can just remove the “additional arc replacements” folder inside the Ghirahim folder you want to use.

You can also independantly choose which form you’d like to use for the Silent Realms, as this uses a different model. There’s 4 different options in total. If you want to say, play as Ghirahim 2nd form during gameplay, but use the Final Form during silent realms, you can just copy the PlLink.arc file from Ghirahim Final Form and put it inside the folder for Ghirahim 2nd form.

Now, for the voice though, it gets... Slightly more tricky. Not by much though. The file named WZSound.brsar needs to be placed inside Actual-Extract > Data > Files > Sound, as well as Modified-Extract > Data > Files > Sound
This is because at the moment, the randomizer does not have a native way to patch in the voice file, so we need to do it this way instead.

That should be all though. If you find anything that’s broken, weird, out of place, or anything else you’d like to provide feedback on, let me know in the comment section, here or on Youtube.
Trailer can be found at: https://youtu.be/ECpYUCqTRVE

Alt Costumes:

This pack includes 6 different versions of Ghirahim to play with.

The 1st form, with and without cape. The 1st form is Ghirahim’s normal form, but it’s easiest to think of it as the version you face at the end of Skyview Temple. By default, he’s going to wear the cape, and if you want him to take off the cape, you can just enable the Skyloft Tunic instead. The randomizer has an option for this under “Tunic Swap”, enable this option if you want him to be capeless.

2nd Form:

The 2nd form, with and without cape. The 2nd form is the version of Ghirahim you fight at the end of the Fire Sanctuary. Same rules apply as 1st form, enable Tunic Swap in the randomizer settings if you want him to be capeless. (Don’t mind the weird wrist on the right hand of the caped version, this is an old screenshot, I already fixed this.)

Final Form

And finally... (Pun intended), Final Form. He doesn’t quite look like he does in the game when you fight him, this is because the playable version lacks all the fancy code the original boss has. I tried, but i was unable to transfer it with the current tools, so at least at the moment, this is what we get. Enable Tunic Swap if you want his core to be fractured... You monster.

That’ll be all. If you want to use another Loftwing model than the one i added, feel free. If you’d like to play without the custom items, feel free. If you have any questions, feel free to hit me up in the comment section and I'll answer best as I can.

Now go wreak havoc on the world as your fabulous Demon Lord self, as you've (probably?) always dreamed of doing.

(Update only fixes the included README.txt and the Ghirahim pictures I put into this description, if you downloaded the mod before there is no need to redownload.)

profile._sText:
WWHD Gameplay & Nintendo HUD patch

This xdelta patch is for the USA/Canada GameCube release of The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker. It is designed and tested for Dolphin. Other GameCube-compatible emulators and modded hardware may work but are currently untested. It embeds the refined grey/white Wind Waker HD-style Nintendo ABXY/ZL/ZR/R HUD, so external textures are not required.

Gameplay changes
- Swift Sail behavior: faster sailing with the wind kept behind the boat.
- Faster dialogue, with B acting as a hold-to-skip button.
- Tingle Chests can be activated with normal bombs and revealed by the compass.
- Successful songs do not play the repeated conducting animation.
- Link can turn while swinging on ropes or the Grappling Hook.
- Shorter Ballad of Gales warp sequence.
- Modern horizontal camera direction.
- Expanded camera range (an additional WWHD-like enhancement).

 HUD changes
- A/B/X/Y button placement, ZR labeling, and D-pad setup.
- Wind Waker HD-style grey/white buttons and lettering.
- Separate A/B action-text spacing to avoid overlap.
- FREE/SELF camera-mode graphics hidden.

Apply the patch
1. Convert a clean USA/Canada RVZ to ISO with Dolphin.
2. Apply `Wind Waker - WWHD Gameplay and Nintendo HUD.xdelta` to that clean ISO with xdelta3 or a compatible xdelta patcher.
3. Optionally convert the patched ISO back to RVZ with Dolphin.

Do not apply the patch directly to an RVZ or to an already modified ISO.

Optional high-resolution HUD textures
For crisper art at high internal resolutions, copy the supplied `NintendoCleanHUD` folder into Dolphin's `Load/Textures/GZL` directory. These textures use hashes unique to the patched ROM and can coexist with Henriko/Hypatia without overwriting that pack's original HUD files.

Young Link sets sail!

Play the GameCube version of The Wind Waker with an adapted Young Link model from Majora's Mask 3D. Includes the green hero outfit, blue lobster-shirt casual outfit, eye tracking, blinking, facial expressions and the existing Young Link voice replacement.

Outfits

Dolphin with native Riivolution support and your own clean USA GameCube copy of The Wind Waker: GZLE01, revision 0. Other regions/revisions and real-console play are not verified.

Disable older Young Link patches and other Link model/voice replacements first. Do not apply this to an already-modded game image. The included README explains the manual XML option. Back up your saves before using mods. Launch without the patch to return to the normal game.

profile._sText:
Sobre o Mod 
Bem-vindos à tradução de The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker para Português de Portugal (PT-PT)! Este projeto nasceu da vontade de trazer uma localização cuidada, natural e imersiva aos jogadores portugueses, corrigindo adaptações antigas e respeitando ao máximo a herança da franquia.

O que está traduzido?

  • Diálogos e Textos: 100% – Toda a história principal, missões secundárias, NPCs, menus e descrições de itens foram adaptados para o português europeu (uso correto do "tu", conjugações e expressões locais).

  • Nota sobre os botões (UI): As indicações dos botões de ação (como os ícones de A, B, R, etc.) não estão traduzidas porque aparecem sob a forma de texturas/imagens diretamente no código do jogo, e não como texto simples. No entanto, todos os diálogos, menus e itens estão perfeitamente localizados!

  • Nomenclatura Fiel: Nomes de personagens, raças e locais foram restaurados para respeitar a versão original em inglês da Nintendo (encontrarás os Rito, os Korok, a Aryll e o Rei dos Leões Vermelhos).

Notas do Criador e Feedback Para agilizar o processo inicial e lidar com o volume massivo de texto, este projeto contou com o apoio de ferramentas de Inteligência Artificial, passando depois por uma revisão para garantir a qualidade. Estou totalmente aberto a sugestões! Se encontrarem alguma frase que possa ser melhorada, aproximada do guião original, ou que beneficie de um vocabulário ainda mais natural em PT-PT, não hesitem em deixar o vosso feedback nos comentários. A vossa ajuda é fundamental para continuar a aperfeiçoar o mod.

Como Instalar Atenção: Em princípio, este mod requer uma cópia Americana (NTSC-U) do jogo para funcionar corretamente. Não foi testado nem é garantido que funcione com as versões Europeia (PAL) ou Japonesa.

Para aplicares esta tradução, vais precisar de substituir um ficheiro dentro da ISO do jogo.

  1. Descarrega a ferramenta GameCube File Tools (GCFT).

  2. Extrai os ficheiros deste mod (o ficheiro que precisas é o bmgres.arc).

  3. Abre a tua ROM/ISO original no GameCube File Tools, (Import GCM), e navega até ao seguinte diretório: files\res\Msg

  4. Substitui o ficheiro bmgres.arc original pelo ficheiro traduzido que descarregaste.

  5. Reconstrói a tua ISO, (Export GCM), guardando as alterações.

  6. Joga a tua nova ROM modificada no teu emulador favorito (como o Dolphin) ou na consola original (através do Nintendont/Swiss)!

profile._sName: Hilda of Lorule: Eye Recolors for the Zelda Skin.
profile._sText:
Zelda's Eye Color only, all other mods pictured are linked below, including the Zelda model by the great "Sir Kilp," which this mod depends on. 

Custom eye colors are configurable in several custom models, but until now, they were not for the amazing playable Zelda- well now with this mod add-on, you can change Zelda's eye color to any color!!

My inspiration for doing this was to make Zelda look like Hilda, the princess of Lorule (with red eyes). Pictures are kinda warped, however it looks flawless in game. 

Prerequisites: 
Find and download Zelda's playable model by google searching: "Windwaker Sage of Mirrors custom models." Zelda is included in the pack, and Sir. Kilp even added hair physics on her main hero outfit! Here is the link to where you download the model pack just in case: 
https://github.com/Sage-of-Mirrors/Custom-Wind-Waker-Player-Models 

The two programs you can choose to download for injecting that Zelda model into your rom are: "Better Windwaker," and/or "Windwaker Randomizer;" both allow custom models to be injected in the exact same way. Better Windwaker is the best way to go if you do not wish to randomize and want to play the vanilla or enhanced game with custom models. Links to the downloads for the programs:
https://github.com/WideBoner/betterww 
https://github.com/LagoLunatic/wwrando 

Installation:
Both Better Windwaker and Windwaker Randomizer tools have an identical folder called "models" inside their respective folders. And in that folder you will put the Sage of Mirror Zelda model's folder you found, called "Zelda." Then in that Zelda folder is where this mod will end up going. Just unzip this mod into the root of the folders for Better Windwaker and/or Windwaker Randomizer, and overwrite the text file it asks to overwrite. 

Done! Now you will have the option to change Zelda's eye color in the programs; this is now also true for her casual outfit's eye color (pony tail)! However, as far as I can see, recoloring only seems to work on one outfit at once. So maybe choose Zelda's outfit you like the most to edit the colors of (Hair down with long dress, or Pony Tail with short dress).The custom eye color might look off-centered within the programs like Better Windwaker and Windwaker Randomizer, but do not fret, in game it will be perfectly applied!

Other mods pictured above:
The other two mods besides Zelda that are pictured are: Ashley from Wario Ware (her book-shield and staff-sword), and the "Dark Linka" mod (Red Ocean). Both of those mods are by the fantastic BigSharkZ. I highly recommend the Dark Linka mod for Hilda, as it is very evil and Lorulean-like; and it even adds evil npcs, and some music from Lorule itself! Both of those mods are linked here, in order:
https://gamebanana.com/mods/250756
https://gamebanana.com/mods/250735

I personally changed the grass texture to purple on the first island, as shown in the pictures; I might add that onto this mod later. I can send you the purple grass textures if you want, just ask me in comments. :) 

How to stack mods:
To combine all of these mods mentioned above into one rom, you can open your rom with the tool "Gamecube File Tools," to add the Ashley model, and the red sea file from the Dark Linka mod for example, or whatever else you want to add like female pronouns, etc. Just make sure you use Gamecube File Tools FIRST, and then use Better Windwaker or Windwaker Randomizer tools SECOND. Link to Gamecube File Tools:
https://github.com/LagoLunatic/GCFT

How to get different character items on Zelda's model:
Each player model sometimes includes custom weapon models, and even custom ship models. Zelda already has super perfect items built into her model, thanks to Sir Kilp going above and beyond here. Her items even include the Bow of Light, and Hilda's actual staff over the skull hammer (how perfect for this)! However, I preferred Ashley's items for Hilda. To achieve this character-item swap, you must first install your custom-player model that has the items you want onto a rom- like Ashley for example.

After this, open the program Better Windwaker or Windwaker Randomizer, and load that new Ashley rom. Now inject the player-model you want to be using the new items, over Ashley's model- so the Zelda model for instance.  When doing this, you must make sure you are checking the box: "Disable Custom Items." That is an essential step for success here. Now you can save your rom, and you are done! This will result in Zelda, with all of Ashley's custom items :) Currently, I cannot combine custom items from both Zelda and Ashley simultaneously, or any two characters- I cannot figure out how. 

Notes:
Again, huge shout-out to Sir Kilp and BigSharkZ for their talent demonstrated in these mods- thank you for making this Lorulean-themed Windwaker possible! Thanks for reading, and feel free to copy my color id's pictured above for a quicker route to the Hilda colors- if you want. Please ask any questions you may have in the comments :) Enjoy!
 

Try out my Hilda reskin, and Red Ocean for Phantom Hourglass as well- linked here: 
https://gamebanana.com/mods/700017

profile._sName: The Legend of Pokémon XD: Wind of Darkness
profile._sText:
NOTE: It is strongly recommended you install The Legend of Pokémon: Actual Sword and Shield first before installing this mod if you want the full experience: https://gamebanana.com/mods/250734

What is The Legend of Pokémon: Wind of Darkness?

It is a mini update/expansion to my mod from 2020, The Legend of Pokémon: Actual Sword and Shield. It includes a few things that I wanted to add in the original release but set aside due to time constraints and shifting focus to other projects.

The main highlight is the addition of Shadow Lugia as a new boss, replacing the Helmaroc King!

But that’s not all, here’s the full list of changes:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 ASM patches:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Centered, larger Dolby (BSZ) logo
  - Skip the game's intro sequence
  - Disabled Link's hand being anchored to the boat tiller
  - Changed Boomerang trail colours to white (for the Poké Ball)
  - Attached the mid-air Deku Leaf particles (004C) to the Deku Leaf's root bone
  - Made the Sail truly invisible (no longer shows up during rainy weather)
  - Forest particles are now pink-lavender instead of green-yellow
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Audio changes:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - New Title Screen song! Based on summoning Lugia in HG/SS and the GS intro
  - Charizard (and by extension Stunfisk) now play Charizard's cry when using the item
  - Helmaroc King's voice clips were fully changed to Lugia's (excluding a few cutscenes)
  - Made Link's voice clip when stabbing Ganondorf silent, to match Red's gameplay voice clips
  - Shadow Mewtwo now has custom voice clips
  - The Lugia boat now has voice clips when enabling / disabling the sail.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Particle changes:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Using Stunfisk now summons dust/smoke particles
  - Charizard now has an actual fire tail!
  - Using Charizard in mid-air spawns ember particles
  - Shadow Lugia now spawns shadow shard particles instead of feathers
  - Breakable wooden bridges now match the darker textures and lighting
  - Title Screen smoke trail is bigger, more spread out and lower to match Shadow Lugia's flight
  - Title Screen wind particles have been changed to twinkling stars
  - Title screen subtitle sparkles have been changed to custom boss warp swirls
  - Shadow Mewtwo now uses two variants of Shadow Ball, including custom impact particles
  - Shadow Mewtwo now has magenta/purple smoke instead of dusty blue
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Actor changes:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Shadow Lugia over Helmaroc King (Including cutscene / resting model)
  - New Forsaken Fortress Tower object textures
  - Forsaken Fortress Tower blue bricks are now Pokémon League statues
  - Shadow Mewtwo's model is now brighter
  - Shadow Mewtwo's Psycho Cut Sword is now shadeless
  - Shadow Mewtwo's particle effects were changed to better suit him
  - Giovanni's robes no longer cull back
  - Giovanni's head is properly centered and no longer stretches weirdly
  - Giovanni now has a proper modeled and rigged neck
  - Slightly redesigned Giovanni's textures
  - Changed Giovanni's cloth material colour from orange to red
  - Newly-improved Charizard model and textures. Charizard no longer has a modeled fire tail
  - Red now has a new animation when riding on his various "boats"
  - Red now has a new animation when riding Charizard
  - Lugia is now a new boat option!
  - New Title Screen logos + Presented by BSZ logo
  - New cutscene edits! Shadow Lugia, Giovanni, Kyogre and Lapras now show up in all cutscenes
  - Animation fix to make Shadow Lugia properly hold Red by the beak
  - Animation fix to make Shadow Lugia properly hold Aryll
  - Animation fix to make Red properly sit on Lapras when first meeting him
  - Cutscene fix to add Wingulls to Aryll being taken by Shadow Lugia
  - Changed Tetra's second model so Bianca now appears in cutscenes
  - Texture fix to remove white outlines from Red's eyes and eyebrows
  - Material fix to make Pokédollar bills show their actual colours on all maps
  - Removed Jabun's lantern effect from Kyogre
  - Removed Jabun's cast light function on Link and the King of Red Lions
  - Fixed Krokorok's head stretching during some animations
  - Rayquaza over the great Valoo (Including cutscene models, but not including Valoo's tail)
  - Fixed a TexMatrixSource issue with Giovanni and Rayquaza.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Map changes:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - New Title Screen background! Also uses the custom forest particles
  - Both instances of the Forsaken Fortress Tower have been retextured to be darker (With a bonus easter egg!)
  - Both instances of the Forsaken Fortress Tower have had their lighting altered to be darker
  - The Forsaken Fortress Tower when fighting Shadow Lugia received a few actor changes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Text changes:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Renamed Helmaroc King to Shadow Lugia
  - Renamed all instances of "King of Red Lions" to "King of Lapras"
  - Renamed all instances of "Boat" to "Pokémon" or "Lapras"
  - Renamed some instances of "Sail" to "HM Surf"
  - Changed one line from "Master of Rocket Fortress" to "Leader of Team Rocket"
  - Changed a bit of Lapras's dialogue
  - Changed all instances of "Valoo" to "Rayquaza"
  - Changed all instances of "Dragon Roost Island" and its variants (Cavern, pond, mountain, etc.) to "Sky Pillar"
  - Added more lore to explain Rayquaza's role and Groudon's disappearance.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 HD textures:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Added HD textures for Charizard, Lugia, Shadow Mewtwo and the Title Screen logo
  - Added optional HD textures for Shiny Charizard, Shiny Lugia, and Pikachu with angry eyes
  - Added vanilla textures for the Boomerang and Deku Leaf particles for users who are using the original TLOP HD texture pack     where they were removed/made invisible.
  - Added new soft shading textures that more accurately keep the original lighting compared to to original mod's
  - Added fixed HD textures for the alternate Red designs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Known issues:
  - King of Red Lions and Valoo show up instead of Lapras and Rayquaza in one cutscene. Unsure of where their models are.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

profile._sText:
Do you want the true definitive save file to just have fun with, and mess around in, but don't have the courage to do it yourself, have already done it and don't want to do it again, or just don't have the time for it? Well, fret no longer! I went and did it myself, manually, sequentially, the intended way, so you don't have to, if you don't want to, or don't have the time for it! If you wanted a save file like that, then this one here, is the one for you! This save file is actually genuinely 100% complete, with nothing major missing, at all, from across the game in its entirety, and the name is actually Link, for those of you who wanted that!

For some context, I noticed that the original GameCube version of this game doesn't have a true 100% save file here on GameBanana, or even across the internet, from what I was able to find, from a lot of thorough researching. There's always something missing, or not completed, in some form, or the name isn't Link, in each and every one of the files I would download, and that was very unfortunate to see, as The Wind Waker is my personal favorite Zelda game, so I took it upon myself to truly 100% the game, in essentially all aspects, with no game breaks, or sequence breaks, playing on Dolphin Emulator on PC, for all to enjoy.

This mod is fully compatible with Dolphin Emulator, which is the recommended way to play the game. The improvements offered in the Better Wind Waker mod on GitHub are just too good to pass up. This is my first ever uploaded mod to a game ever. Enjoy it as you please!
If you're wondering why Link looks different and more classic, and why the title screen says "Wind Waker HD" in the screenshots I posted, it's because I'm using Better Wind Waker, a modified, enhanced, and, well, better version of the game ISO, more akin to the Wii U version of the game, that you can find and download for free from GitHub, to change how my Link looks, and I'm also using the Hypatia HD Texture Pack, to make the game just look so much better and much more up to date, and higher quality, for today's standards.

I highly recommend playing the game today with the Better Wind Waker mod that is freely available on GitHub, for the definitive experience, though it's not required, just immensely recommended! It enhances the game in just about every way, so drastically, and significantly, to the point where once you use it, you'll genuinely feel like you can't go back to the regular default version of the game!
I completed essentially everything in the game, from start to finish, on 1st quest, with Link's green tunic, as well as 2nd quest, with Link's blue Island Lobster shirt, and the name is Link on all files, so anyone playing can comfortably use this as their own file, and choose which outfit for Link they want to play with, and mess around with, and just have fun. There's even a 3rd file, also named Link, set at Hyrule Castle, before the barrier is broken later in the game, so you can freely use that file to practice the famous barrier skip glitch, and mess around with the barrier like jumping over it, with the moon jump gecko code.

In this save file, the main story is completed, all sidequests are completed, the Deluxe Pictobox has been collected in the 1st quest, which carries over to the 2nd quest, the Nintendo Gallery is completed in the 1st quest, all figurines are there, which carries over to the 2nd quest too, all items are collected, Magic Armor included, all songs are learned, all heart pieces are collected, all treasure charts are collected, the treasure from said treasure charts are collected, all 60 points have been earned in Beedle's shop membership, and the Silver and Gold membership cards have been collected as a result of such.

The Hero's Charm has been collected, the hurricane spin is learned, all the big Octos have been defeated, all Island squares have been mapped out by the Fishman, all the submarines have been found and completed, all 23 blue Chuchu have been collected, max 99 Joy Pendants have been given to Mrs. Marie, all the upgrades are collected and maxed out, including the wallet that goes up to 5000, bomb bag that goes up to 99, and quiver that goes up to 99, from the various fairy fountains. All 4 of the bottles are collected, one is filled with a full bottle of Grandma's Elixir Soup, with the other 3 having half a bottle of Elixir Soup, using the famous soup glitch.

There are max 5000 rupees, all spoils bag items are collected, there are max 99 arrows and bombs, the bait bag is filled with an equal amount of bait and hyoi pears, all dungeons are fully completed, with all the chests in each of them being found and opened, except for the one in Dragon Roost Cavern, by the boss door, purposely so that you can practice and try the famous storage glitch, for fun. I thought that keeping that one in would be a nice idea, since you can only open a chest once, and after it's been opened, it stays opened forever. You can open that chest in both files if you'd like to though, of course.

All the hidden Tingle statues in all the dungeons are found, both Windfall Island and Link's Oasis are fully decorated, with only the Hero's Flag from the Guru shop on Windfall Island that you receive from completing the trading sequence side quest, and the potion shop at Windfall Island is completed too. The Hero's Flag is my personal favorite one to decorate with, which is why I used it, but you can change that to your own liking with your own favorite if you want that, of course.

This is the absolute definitive save file for the original GameCube version of The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker that you will find online! It took a fairly long while to complete, it was fun to do, beyond enjoyable, and I'm very proud of it! I was glad to do it for others, not just for myself! It was awesome! Have fun with it! May the fortune of the wind be with you!
Installation Instructions:
An extraction tool like WinRAR, which is free, is required to extract the file! To apply the save file to Dolphin Emulator for use, using the default GCI folder to save with for GameCube games, simply go to File Explorer, on your PC, then your PC drive in "This PC", like the Windows (C:) drive, then Users, then your PC's name, then AppData, then Roaming, then Dolphin Emulator, then GC, then your country (USA, JAP, or EUR), then Card A, then place the file in there, and it will properly function in the game. Enjoy!

If all this is too confusing, you can also just simply right click on the game in Dolphin Emulator on the screen that shows your game list, then go to "Open GameCube Save Folder" to get there faster, and that's where that extracted file goes. Enjoy!

FAQ:
Q: His head is pretty stiff, why does he sometimes not look at things?
A: Dampe uses Link's original bones/skeleton so I'm limited to the original animations. Since Link wasn't a hunchback, lots of animations looked bad if the head was fully animated. Lots of stretching and awkward poses.

Q: Where are the weapon sheaths, and why does the stick and shovel not appear on Dampe's back?
A: Dampe's huge back clipped into where the sheath model would be and was distractingly bad looking. Just hiding it was the easiest and cleanest solution without compromising Dampe's original model.

Q: The halo can droop?
A: For the reasons in question one, Dampe's head is technically just Link's neck, and the halo is his head. I like how the halo bobs somewhat independently from his head at the cost of sometimes the head animation making the halo turn to look at something his modeled "head" is not.
