Have You Ever Wanted to Immerse Yourself as an Indentured Servant?

I haven't, but now you can!


This model swap was made for Aproxm’s The Wind Waker: Rewritten ROM hack. As it’s his "worker’s attire," I dirtied it up quite a bit by painting sweat marks and stains on the torso. I wanted to add stubble to the chin to make him more gnome-like, but the face texture is overlapped onto his hands, which made them look hairy—ew. Maybe I’ll find a fix and make a stubble variant, but for now, he’s clean-shaven. His flaccid gnome hat is stained and crinkled, and because I propped it upwards, it stiffens up depending on certain wind conditions—it’s like it has a mind of its own. I am not fixing it because it looks funny.
Anyways, here's the concept art I based it off of-- you can find it on his website.






Tutorial (Stolen From the Randomizer Skin Pack)

No, you don't have to use it with Wind Waker Rewritten and yes it's available on official hardware.

Requirements:
  • Dolphin Emulator.
  • A "legal" copy of a Wind Waker ISO.

Extracting your ISO:
This mod is easier to install with an extracted Wind Waker ISO. It makes editing individual files easier, and you won't have to worry about injecting files directly into the ISO.
  1. Open Dolphin, right click your Wind Waker ISO, and click on Properties. Go to the Filesystem tab.
  2. Right click on Disc, and click Extract Entire Disc, and choose a new folder in an easily accessible location. (I.E. "C:\Users\John Doe\Documents\Dolphin Emulator\ISOs\LOZWW".)
  3. Click on Configure, and go to the Paths tab. Make sure your LOZWW folder is added to the ISO directories.
  4. Add the path for dolphin to find the boot.dol you just extracted.
  5. The game should appear in the game list, but with 0 bytes of data. This is normal. You can now open it like any other game.

Installing the Model:
  1. In your extracted models folder, open the folder of the model you would like to use.
  2. Create a backup of Link.arc located in "files\res\Object" of the extracted game files.
  3. Replace the vanilla Link.arc with the modded one.
The model was made with a combination of SuperBMD (@SageOfMirrors) and WW Model Helper Scripts (@LagoLunatic).

profile._sText:
The Goose is Loose and ready to honk and spread chaos across Hyrule!
After 4 years, I am finally releasing a new mod. Time sure flies like a goose!

This is a mod pack that originally started as a simple Link replacement, requested by Crain from The Wind Waker Randomizer and Racing communities, back in 2022.

However, I enjoyed working on the mod so much that I expanded it into a large mod pack with a lot of changes, taking months of work to complete.

What does this mod include?

---------------------
 ~ Alternate Files ~
---------------------
These contain alternate / extra files that aren't a part of the main pack.

- Butter Knife:
Replaces the Hero's Charm, which is normally the Master Sword.

- Jumping instead of rolling:
Makes the goose jump instead of roll when pressing A. Also changes the goose's running and autojump speed.

- King of Red Lions with Crown & Sunglasses:
Replaces the Lily Pad boat with the King of Red Lions wearing a crown and sunglasses.

- Honk-on-command Alternate Files
Contains alternate patches to go alongside the honk-on-command patch.

- No Shading:
Disables the game's shading like Untitled Goose Game.

- Soft Shading:
Changes the game's shading to be softer, blurrier.

- Randomizer-only Sound Files
Sound files that you can use if you just want to play with the goose without the full mod pack.
Custom animations (LkAnm.arc) are still recommended to use in that case.

- Superswim Fix:
Disables the camera change when using the Wind Waker, for those who want to do the superswim glitch.
---------------------
    ~ Full Pack ~
---------------------
The full mod pack! Avoid reading if you don't want any spoilers on its contents.

It includes:

- Custom asm:
Bigger, centered Dolby logo (Replaced with my own logo)
Running animations have a closed mouth
Wind Waker particle effects that follow Link's hands are removed (But not those from conducted notes)
Magic Armour lighting fix (Makes it properly use toon shading)
Invisible Hookshot chain
Brown Boomerang trail colour
Removed black and white effect from Hyrule
Invisible sail (Unless using the King of Red Lions)
Honk-on-command (Press d-pad left to honk!)

- Custom audio:
Goose voice pack
Honk Waker over the Wind Waker
Title Screen custom music
Tale of the Legendary Goose (New Prologue)
Helmaroc King cutscene custom audio (When it throws Link far away into the sea)

- Rel files:
Edited Ganondorf rel file to remove the orange strings attached to his swords

- Msg files:
Acticon.arc (Replaces a few text prompts such as "Attack" or "Call" with "Honk")
Bmgres.arc (Adds custom text for characters like Ganondorf, Grandma, Sturgeon, Orca and Abe, Outset and Windfall NPCs, Medli,

island names, No Goose Signs, changes Rupees to Coins, Ghost Ship to Goose Ship, etc.)
Fmapres.arc (Changes Rupee icon to Coin icon)
Menures.arc (Changes button icons to orange, Heart icons to Bells)

Note that the custom text does not apply to the entire game, just most of what is encountered in a Randomizer run. You can still play the mod in vanilla The Wind Waker without issues, however.

- Object files:
Always.arc (Changes pots to vases, Mirror Shield reflection to the goose, the camera icon, targeting icon, ruppe model, etc.)
Am2.arc (Changes Armos to Jeremy Fish)
Bgn.arc (Changes Puppet Ganon to look like the Old Man)

Demo43.arc (Changes the Ganondorf statue into the Old Man's, a Goose Allowed Sign over the Master Sword, a new stylish look for the King of Hyrule and changes to the Goose and Zelda's bubble models)
Demo51.arc (Changes to the Title Screen camera to keep it static)
Other Demo arc files (Changes Ganondorf and King models)

Logo.arc (Changes the Dolby logo to my own logo)
Md.arc (Changes Medli's animations so she can ride the Goose, also gave her a happy mouth)

Pz.arc (Changes Zelda's dress colours and adds the Player 2 Goose on top of her head)

- Particle files:

Room11.arc (Adds a new island name to Windfall Island, the Secret Map entrance, a Soccer Ball, and No Goose signs, etc.)

profile._sText:
--------------------------------------
THE LEGEND OF KRYSTAL - THE WIND WAKER
--------------------------------------

Mod by AngelTheVixen, version 1.01b

This mod is intended for use with the GameCube version of The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker, specifically with the game code GZLE01.

--------------------------------------
             INTRODUCTION
--------------------------------------

Thanks for downloading my mod! As a Krystal and Dinosaur Planet obsessor, it brings me great joy to offer this little mod to you and your enjoyment. Finally, Krystal of Animus can have her own, whole and complete adventure.

--------------------------------------
            HOW TO INSTALL
--------------------------------------

Below are the instructions to install and play!

Both a complete mod with additional changes and a standalone model compatible with the Randomizer are available.

Full Mod

A - Standard - Install through GameCube File Tools.

1) Download the program GameCube File Tools by LagoLunatic, found at:
https://github.com/LagoLunatic/GCFT
If you're unfamiliar with GitHub, look on the side of the page for Releases and download the appropriate package.

2) Acquire a vanilla, unmodified ISO of the North American version of The Wind Waker, the game's internal label should be GZLE01.

3) Run GameCube File Tools.

4) Select 'Import GCM', and import the ISO.

5) Select 'Replace All Files in GCM'.

6) Find the mod folder, and click on the 'Full Mod' folder. Confirm with Select Folder, and make sure it's not for any of the folders inside of it.

7) The files will be replaced. Select 'Export GCM' and save the patched copy.

8) Enjoy Krystal's adventure!

B - Advanced - Install by replacing existing files.

If you have an ISO, Dolphin allows you to right click on a game > Properties > Filesystem > Extract Entire Disc. You can then adjust the emulator's config to add the extracted game folder to the game paths. Dolphin will be able to run a game in its entirety through folders rather than disc images with this method.

Once the game is dumped into folders for use in Dolphin, you can use this simple replacement method.

It is highly suggested to make a full copy of the game into another folder as a backup. Then, you can insert the folders from the Full Mod folder and overwrite the same folders of the vanilla Wind Waker. When that's all done, you'll be able to play!

Randomizer Pack

This mod comes with a Randomizer-compatible package for your Rando enjoyment, so you can send her on one confusing mess of an adventure.

Her textures have been simplified to allow for color changes, have fun with making your own vixen!

To install, all you have to do is place the 'Krystal (Dinosaur Planet)' folder into the 'models' folder for the Randomizer, and restart the Randomizer. It's simple as that!

--------------------------------------
          TOTAL MODIFICATIONS
--------------------------------------

 - Title screen logo changed.
 - Link replaced.

This is for the USA version & BetterWW. I added Xdelta patches to it in a folder to make things easier. I believe in M_NewD2 you can copy the Stage.arc and some of the rooms I modded like Room0, 2, 3, 5, & 12 into the Japanese Stage folder. For Siren, you can just copy Room0.arc only. I did test some stages in the Europe version and they worked.

I fixed a bug in Outset from my previous version where the wooden boarded up wall would be in the scene in the Aryll kidnapping cutscene. AA stands for added actors in my title. In my new rar file, I fix the unused enemy boat's switch flag in three eye isle so it doesn't conflict with that other island with the golden boat. So anyways, I restore the Floormasters in FF1 and add some candles in FF1 and FF2. In FF1 in the inside, I restore a unused table and its other actors that go with it. I add back the Octorocks in the Tower of the Gods as well as a switch that triggers a unused red rupee pot. In the Wind Temple for room 2, I add back that iron boots switch that triggers the joy pendant chest as well as unused makar plants from cave 08. (Update) I forgot to change the joy pendant chest in the Wind Temple so it spawns with the switch in my 3 previous versions. So the 4th one fixes that. I also add back the 3 peahats and the 2 moving spike machines in room 2 from cave 08. In Outset, I add 3 pots near Orca's house as well as the unused Weak boarded up wall up the hill. I changed Dragon Roost Cavern so some rooms are like the E3 version when it comes to the actors. My DRC changes are all fanmade though since I added those actors. The unused cutscenes where I added a event trigger actor are in the game's data though. In cave 03 or the underground forest area, I added the unused Spike Tentacle Blockage from layer 7 to the default layer. In Orca's house upstairs, I put some actors from layer 7 I think to the default layer so they load. Also included 2 pots near the window but I had to move them. In Puppet Ganon's boss room, I restored some unused platforms and the plants. The plants are those shooting things Link can jump in. In the unused K_test 2, I put the layer 7 unused actors to the default layer. In the sailing minigame, the npc is loaded. In the unused ktest e, I restore the 2 seagull actors. In Outset Island, I restore a tree, some items Link can get on those boats later in the game, and some enemies. In Forsaken Fortress 2, I restore the floormaster. The other floormaster and the box actors were added in since it made sense. In Dragon Roost island, I restore 4 rocks as well as a tingle pot. 

In Forest Haven, I restore a bush, a octorock, and a tingle pot. I don't want to say where the tingle pots are though. You'll have to find that for yourself. In the new rar files, I add some unused actors in the Ghost Ship, the unused ghost ship, and Abship room 4. Abship room 4 is the area with the pigs and ropes to get across to the chest. Its in that submarine. I also put sea room 45 in the folder as a optional room to use since it restores a unused korok and his tree on Headstone Island. The bmgres.arc file adds a Japanese sound 47 for Mila. I'm unsure if it works though as the sound could of been removed. The new version also has the Layer 8 actors which are unused in the default layer for the unused ghost ship maps in Sub Dungeon 71 and 45. The other Pship rooms have the restored actors as well from layer 8. The newest version makes Outset's title screen match some of the unused actors from the regular room 44 Outset. You don't have to use the optional outset island folder or the Prerelease Ganon M & J folder. The outset island ones are my old versions. So anyways, this new version has the unused keeses and unused seagulls In Outset and Windfall Island. I had to move the Unused Keeses more towards the middle of the destroyed bridge area so Link could hit them. Fixed a bug in Ganon K or the Ganon Boss room so the eye switch doesn't trigger the stalfos in Ganon E or the Ganon Earth Temple room. Restore flame actors in Link's Oasis so they appear at night. In newest version, fixed the green rupee flags in Forbidden Wood's miniboss room. Restored the 4 barrels in the pirate ship in the beginning of the game. Restored some pirate crates and a barrel in the bomb shop. In WarpD or the Pirate Ship chart cave, I restored 5 of the 6 actors. The 2 I restore in the 1st folder are a large pot and a floormaster. The 2nd WarpD folder has those 2 actors and 3 Warp Pots. I decided not to use the Pink Warp so I put it in layer 8. The Siren and M_NewD2 with the unused rooms loaded through winditor folders, they can load the unused rooms in The tower of the gods and Dragon Roost Cavern with winditor. You can't access those rooms in normal gameplay though. I added a "unused Grotto in sea areas and in Hyrule" folder so you can explore some unused rooms. I did want to include beta fire mountain but I would have to change the chest content since I can't have 2 rooms with power bracelets. (Update) That is in Part 2. Part 1 folder was removed in the latest version to make the rar size smaller. In Outset Island or room 44 in the sea folder, I could of restored that one Palm Tree in layer 11 that was in front of Orca's house but I didn't as it seemed like it would be in the way & it may not look good to look at the house at a far distance.

In my most recent rar file of the rooms and stages in the folder, "M_NewD2 Updated with startcam cutscene and cliff 2 cutscene, plus the unused bridge 00 event too (has Moribomb CS)", you can just copy the rooms that don't have the long names as some are newer then the ones with the long names. You could use that stage one that says "before added Palettes for Room 3" if you don't want the added 2 colors at certain times of the day which is a total of 6. In the final, it only uses 4 colors or something for some areas.

Credits for the bmgres.arc files for the fast text/instant text go to Wind Waker Randomizer & Better Wind Waker. I edited the Better Wind Waker one though. And restore Mila's unused Goodbye sound & the other file adds the "Then hang on tightly!" unused text that was said by the King of Red Lion's. And credits go to Twili13, Flotonic, Blank, Kargaroc, jaytheham, and Cuber456 for "The_Wind_Waker_HACK_US (3) Fixed" folder with the stages. I fixed stuff with the maps. I know they all worked on the AR00 map which is that beta Spaceworld forest map shown in beta trailers.

profile._sText:
Hello! After some time working on it, I finally got it finished.
So here's Metroid Fusion's Samus, with some of her equipment, ready to kick some bokoblins' asses!
She lost all her items while getting ported to Wind Waker, but hey, she will recover them (as always). 
The list of items she wants back:

- The powerful, upgradeable Beam Blade!
- The grapple beam from Metroid Prime!
- Her special super missiles! (she refuses to use her arm cannon to actually shoot until she gets those back)
- The (huge) power bombs! 
- The literal Screw Attack upgrade (I guess she didn't want to install the app via her USB cannon...)
- Ridley's frozen, severed head! (geez)
- Kraid's claw (one of them, at least)
- No shields! She, uh, she just decides to block with her arm cannon. And uh, she cleans it in order to make it so shiny it reflects light, I guess
- A lost friend! That's up to you to find who he or she is ;)

This was my first mod ever, and I tried so hard for it to not have any bugs. However, I can list some I just wasn't able to correct; and if you find some more, tell me!
List of known errors:
- When she has low health, some weird positioning occurs. To fix it I would need to change Samus' head animation over to Link's hat; that would make her head bobble and wiggle. And that's even weirder.
- I have tried to cover it up, but since Samus' hand doesn't fit with Link's, there might be some instances of the hand disconnecting from the arm.
- Great fairies appearing and disappearing sounds and bombs vanished?? I don't seem to know why that is, but I'm trying to fix it.
- Randomizer colors look buggish, with the original texture clipping over the masked textures. I had to recreate preview images from scratch since the script provided by the otherwise great tutorial by LagoLunatics didn't work. However, in-game textures look great.

Thanks to my friend Rodri who supported me from the beggining :)

profile._sName: Skyward Ascent - Rando Support for SS Link
profile._sText:
First off, thanks to Skilar for letting me use his awesome Skyward Sword Link model in a randomizer mod! I absolutely loved it when I first found it, and was sad when I found it was only made for vanilla. I started making a voice replacement to accompany it, but Skilar gave me permission to use the model as well!

Features

  • An edited version of Skilar's Skyward Sword Link model that is fully compatible with the randomizer and has fingerless gloves!
  • Full support for Dolphin Emulator (tested using Latest Beta) and Original Hardware (tested using Nintendont on a 1st-gen Wii and a Family Edition Wii)
  • Full custom color support for Hero's Clothes
  • Two options for custom voicelines that cover all of Link's non-cutscene sounds

Changes from Skilar's version:

  • Casual Clothes are disabled since they would need several additional UV mapping adjustments. I may add this at some point, but have no plans to at the moment.
  • The Hero's Clothes texture has had any artifacting removed and has less compression in-game. 
  • Due to redone UV mapping for the Hero's Clothes, Link's hair only supports a single, solid color
  • I added fingerless gloves to make the mod more closely resemble Skyward Sword Link. Big thanks to BigSharkZ for all their help with this!

Voice Options

  • Normal/Original - Unedited voice clips from Skyward Sword
  • Higher/Adjusted - Equivalent voice clips from Skyward Sword with 9% higher pitch to sound like a younger hero

Installation

Extract the contents of the .7z file to your models folder. If using both, the models will not override each other and will instead appear as separate options.

profile._sText:
The previous mod was deleted by an admin instead of being moved to this GUI category so here is a re-upload, sorry about that.

This is a custom HUD that I made as part of the Winds of Time project, which aims to replicate the OoT HUD in The Wind Waker. Make sure to read everything thoroughly before reporting anything or asking any questions.

There are 4 different styles to choose from:

- The Wind Waker Style with GC Colors
- The Wind Waker Style with N64 Colors
- Ocarina of Time Style with GC Colors
- Ocarina of Time Style with N64 Colors

Feel free to pick the one you like the most!

Note that each style will use the same custom Heart Pieces, Magic Meter and Rupee icons.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
How to install
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Download GCFT here: https://github.com/LagoLunatic/GCFT/releases
2. Open GCFT and click "Import GCM" to import your vanilla ISO or Randomizer seed.
3. Navigate to Files > res > Msg.
4. Right-click on "menures.arc" and select "Replace File".
5. Choose the custom HUD file you want to use.
6. Export your ISO by clicking on "Export GCM".

Note: You can also do this with your generated seed for the Randomizer as the Randomizer itself does not mess with menures.arc. This is unlike some of my past mods where the vanilla ISO needs to be modified first.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Known issues:
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- A button moves out of the screen and appears cut off during cutscenes where the user is able to press A. Cannot fix.

- Setting items on X, Y and Z will have the animation still try to move them to the original HUD positions. Cannot fix.

- The text on the A and B buttons is not always in the same position depending on the word. Vanilla behavior.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F.A.Q.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q: Will this HUD work with the vanilla game?
A: Yes.

Q: Will this HUD also work with the Randomizer?
Q: Also yes.

Q: During cutscenes, the A button icon is cut off and pokes through the top of the screen, is that normal?
A: Yes, as of right now there is nothing I can do to fix this.

Q: Does this include the Winds of Time item icons?
A: No, this is just a release for the custom HUD. Item icons might be released alongside the Link mod.

Q: What did you use to create this?
A: I used arookas's BLO tools which you can find here: https://github.com/arookas/blojob/releases

Q: I have an issue to report that is not listed here, how can I contact you?
A: Feel free to drop a message and ping me in the Wind Waker Randomizer Discord Server, or post a comment on the GameBanana page or my YouTube channel.

Enjoy!
~BigSharkZ

profile._sText:
This is a very simple skin that alters the skin color of Princess Zelda's model to match that of Tetra's, for obvious reasons.  Having played a whole lot of WWR on console recently, I was tired of reaching the final battle only to fight beside an incredibly pale Zelda - so, I decided to do something about it!

Credit for the altered textures themselves goes fully to Hypatia, who gave me full permission to upload this mod here.  I am responsible only for downscaling the textures and injecting them in a way that will work on console.

(Note:  Though the Wind Waker Randomizer allows players to alter the colors of the player model, including custom ones, this is NOT a skin for the custom, playable Zelda model you can download for the randomizer.  This is a skin for the non-playable Zelda you fight Ganondorf alongside at the end of the game.)

YOU WILL NEED:

  • LagoLunatic's GameCube File Tools
  • an ISO of the original game

INSTALL INSTRUCTIONS:

  1.  download the included .zip and extract the "Pz.arc" file anywhere on your desktop
  2.  in GameCube File Tools, under the "GCM ISOs" tab, click "Import GCM" in the upper left and navigate to wherever your vanilla TWW ISO is located; select and open it
  3.  find the original Pz.arc file (path is "files/res/Object/Pz.arc"), right-click and select "Replace File," and navigate to wherever you extracted the modded file from step one
  4.  export the newly modded ISO ("Export GCM") to wherever you like (it is NOT recommended that you save over the original ISO! either save the new one in a new location or rename it so you know which one it is!)
  5.  use the modded ISO to generate your randomizer seeds, and voila! you did it :))

Please also note that if you're playing TWW or its ranodmizer on Dolphin, it is much easier to simply load custom textures in order to achieve the same effect (check out Hypatia's High-Res Wind Waker Texture Pack, linked above).  I made this mod as I load WWR through Nintendont on a homebrewed Wii (which doesn't allow the loading of custom textures).

profile._sName: Dark Linka & The King's Revenge (Mod Pack)
profile._sText:
NOTE: The texture pack is mandatory and not optional as of right now, please follow the instructions thoroughly; if the game says "Randomizer" instead of "Dark Linka Edition", you do not have it installed. This is mentioned because of many users who have forgotten the last steps.

At last, it's finally here! This is a mod pack that has been in the works for 4 months, if not more. Hundreds of hours were poured into this project, so I hope you will enjoy it as I take a break from WW modding.

Now, what is this pack? You may be familiar with my Linka mod, which became a lot more popular than I expected it to be. My own take on a female Link, I enjoyed the creative process so much, that combined with all the requests I got to make more Linka content, I decided to do a mod pack about a new character: Dark Linka.

It includes a new story and lore, new textures, models, voice clips, menus, HUD, animations, maps, lighting, and even a custom soundtrack with 35 new songs!

Before we get started, make sure to look at the attached instructions on this page, which can also be found in the README. This is a lot of info, but it will make sure you understand what this includes, and how to use it properly. Note that there is a 50-image limit, so I cannot show all that this pack contains. There will eventually be a showcase video in the future, so I hope you look forward to it!

I recommend not using Randomized Enemy Colors the first time you play the mod, as that setting will change the palettes of my custom enemies and bosses.

It was also reported that the game may hang in the last room of the extra dungeon. I cannot replicate it, but a simple fix is to click "Ignore" when the error pops up on Dolphin.
EDIT: That crash should now be gone. Let me know if it still occurs!
------------------------------------------------------------
INSTRUCTIONS (Follow in order, do not forget the texture pack!)
------------------------------------------------------------
GCFT Download: https://github.com/LagoLunatic/GCFT/releases
Randomizer Download: https://github.com/LagoLunatic/wwrando

(NOTE: There is a bug with the 1.8.0 version of the Randomizer where it cannot randomize if the base ISO contains a modified ship.arc, and the model folder has the exact same file.
To fix it, simply remove "ship.arc" from her Randomizer folder, or from the Dark Linka Pack folder, in files/res/Object)
------------------------------------------------------------
Dark Linka Pack folder installation:
------------------------------------------------------------
1. With your vanilla ISO opened in GCFT, click "Import Folder over GCM".
2. Navigate inside the Dark Linka Pack folder, click anywhere but on "files",  just be in the Dark Linka Pack folder. Click Open and it should install the mod almost instantly.
3. In GCFT, navigate to Files > res > Stage > Ojhous2.
4. Right-click on Ojhous2 and click "Add File".
5. Navigate to Dark Linka Pack > files > res > Stage > Ojhous2.
6. Select Room2.arc and add the file.
7. Repeat the same process but with Room8.arc and Room9.arc.
8. Right-click on Stage and select "Add Folder" (Only available on GCFT 1.8.0)
9. Type "Ojtrain" without the quotation marks, following the capitalization.
10. Scroll down and navigate to Ojtrain, right-click it and select "Add File".
11. In the Dark Linka Pack, navigate to Files > res > Stage > Ojtrain.
12. Add Room0.arc and Stage.arc to the Ojtrain folder you created.
13. Export the ISO as a new one with any name you like!
------------------------------------------------------------
Randomizer folder installation:
------------------------------------------------------------
NOTE: You can ONLY randomize over the mod pack, and not the other way around where you install the mod pack over a randomized ISO.

1. Place the "Dark Linka" folder inside the "models" folder of the Randomizer.
2. Take a look at the "Casual Presets" and "Hero Presets" image files to pick a palette that you like, though this is optional if you want her normal look.
3. Launch the Randomizer and in the Player Customization tab, select the Dark Linka mod.
4. Wait about 15-20 seconds as it loads the mod.
5. If you want a custom palette, from the palette drop down you can pick any that I made, I don't recommend setting every color manually since you will have to wait each time you change colors.
(If you truly want your own palettes, open metadata.txt in her model folder and delete all the presets, while keeping the base color data at the very top)
6. Once the mod and / or palette is selected, go back to the first tab.
7. For "Clean WW ISO", select the new ISO you created with GCFT.
8. For "Output Folder", select the folder where your Randomized ISO will be generated.
9. Seed name can be anything, clicking "New seed" will generate a random name, but you can write your own too.
10. Click "Randomize", wait until it completes the process!
------------------------------------------------------------
Texture Pack installation:
------------------------------------------------------------
(This is assuming you are using a dev build of Dolphin, and not stable or beta as the paths are different and some issues may be present with a non-development build)
1. Go inside the "Texture Pack" folder and select all folders
2. In a new window, navigate to (Drive) > Users > (User) > Documents > Dolphin Emulator > Load > Textures.
3. Create a folder named "GZLE99" without the quotation marks.
4. Place the folders that were inside "Texture Pack" inside the GZLE99 folder.
5. In Dolphin, click "Graphics" at the top.
6. Click on the last tab, "Advanced".
7. Check "Load Custom Textures" and then close the window.
8. Launch the game! If all goes well, you should have many custom textures, a quick test is to check the title screen and make sure it says "Dark Linka Edition".

If the textures do not load, look at your paths in Dolphin's settings to see if you are using a different path than the default one, or if OneDrive changed the paths.
------------------------------------------------------------
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Who is Dark Linka?
~ A: Dark Linka is a different take on my Linka mod; a girl that comes from a darker, corrupted timeline.

Her name is actually Kirie, in similar fashion to Ravio not having the same name as Link in ALBW.
However she decided to give up on her former identity when she met the pure-hearted Linka, and always tries to be one step ahead of her.

While Linka travels through timelines for research purposes and to help as many people as she can find, Dark Linka hops through timelines for fun, stealing all sorts of powerful items and relics or facing new challenges to avoid boredom.

She holds no remorse for her actions as she considers all of this a mere game, but is "evil" in an innocent way.

To contrast Linka using heroic or cute items that she finds on her travels, Dark Linka uses darker items, or items that strong characters and villains used throughout the Zelda series, that she snatches without permission.

Her boat, the Prince of Dark Dragons, is someone she met in one of those timelines, who seeks revenge on the King of Hyrule, who took over his land. Considering Dark Linka's immense strength and her ability to hold and control powerful artifacts such as Majora's Mask, this dark boat accompanies her in order to find the Dark Triforce, an artificial relic that is said to rival the power of the Gods.

Who is this prince, anyway? You'll have to find out when you beat the game!
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: What is this timeline? Everything is so dark and spooky!
A: This is a timeline where dark energy influenced the natural order of life. Ganondorf was sealed away, yet there is no hero to be found...
Many inhabitants of the original timeline simply evolved into a darker version of themselves, whereas other characters like Link and Grandma simply do not exist... or they passed away.
However, one person is determined to bring light and order back. It's up to Dark Linka to stop that from happening!
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Is this mod compatible with the vanilla game, or is it Randomizer only?
~ A: Randomizer only. This is because I have removed certain story events for memory optimization, and also completely changed important maps such as Orca's house.
Furthermore, changing the entire game's script and cutscenes to reflect my story / mod would take an insane amount of work and I just do not have the time for it.
The Randomizer removes a lot of text and cutscenes and so I worked with what was left for a more streamlined experience.
Lastly, many of the item pickups I added will only appear in the Randomizer as they were not programmed to appear in the vanilla game.

It is possible to play the mod with the vanilla game if some files are removed, but I still do not recommend it, any issues will be for you to figure out.
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Is this mod playable on consoles?
~ A: Unfortunately not at the moment, due to an issue with custom indoor locations not working on original hardware.
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Did you make this entire mod all by yourself?
~ A: I did! However, it would not have been possible without the help and tools of many people in the community, as well as the support of many friends.
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: I have a crash and I'm stuck! What do I do?
~ A: As of this mod's release, there should not be any crashes left. However, the memory usage in this game can be pretty odd and hard to figure out at times..
Please report the crash to me, either on the mod's download page, or in the WWR Discord Server! I will do my best to figure it out.

If you crash in "Shark's Trial" on the last room, simply click "Ignore" on the message that pops up. That error should have been fixed but could still happen.

Alternatively, you can use a debug map select code to warp into the room you need to access. There should only be crashes in Forsaken Fortress and Hyrule which I also have fixed.
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: I cannot Randomize the ISO! I get a "Randomization failed with error: 'FileEntry' object has no attribute 'image_format'". How come?
~ A: This is an issue with the Randomizer that was fixed and will be included in the next version. Until then, make sure you only have one "ship.arc" file, either in the Dark Linka Pack folder, or the Randomizer model folder.
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Why is the Randomizer stuck when selecting Dark Linka?
~ A: This is another issue with the Randomizer due to her large amount of color presets.
It can take from 5 seconds to 20 seconds to load depending on your computer, therefore I recommend using one of the color presets I made, or using none.
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Can I use Dark Linka on her own without the mod pack?
A: Yes! Simply use the Randomizer folder and do not install the pack with GCFT.
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Can I use a specific file only, such as the Lizalfos, or the custom soundtrack without the other changes?
A: Also yes! You can insert any specific files manually over your ISO with GCFT with the "Replace File" option.
The soundtrack is located in files/Audiores/Seqs/JaiSeqs.arc, for other files you can refer to these lists:

Actor list:
https://github.com/LordNed/Winditor/blob/master/Editor/resources/ActorDatabase_orig.json

Map lists:
https://github.com/LordNed/WindEditor/wiki/Map,-Island,-and-Object-Names
https://github.com/LagoLunatic/wwrando/blob/master/data/stage_names.txt
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Why wasn't (example) changed? Are there things that cannot be changed?
~ A: Yes, mostly content that the Randomizer adds on top of my mod. There are also some issues that cannot be fixed at the moment, here is a list:

- Takkuri texture issue on Revenant Island: Does not always happen, is memory-related.
- Camera angle after defeating the final boss: Stb cutscene files cannot be edited yet.
- Final boss turning to stone has a quick / jarring animation: Cannot be fixed, issue with the repacking process.
- Poe soul texture sometimes appears incorrect and is duplicated: No idea why it happens, rare issue.
- "The sea is yours" text refers to Ganondorf, despite him not being the final boss: Randomizer-only text, cannot fix.
- The "Shadow Sail" is named the "Swift Sail": Randomizer-only text, cannot fix.
- Rylla (Aryll) calls Dark Linka "brother": Randomizer-only text, cannot fix.
- Weird bubble after the final battle that stays stationary, and Dark Linka's eyes get messed up: Issue with the repacking process, cannot fix.
- Poe Soul is named "Key Bag": Randomizer-only text, cannot fix.
- Free items such as Magic Armor or Power Bracelets may eventually disappear / become unavailable, won't fix.
- Narwa can get stuck behind a torch, giving tons of free hits if using jump slashes. Intended.

If you find anything else that isn't listed here, let me know!
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: Why is there a big shark when swimming?
~ A: I can't believe I'm putting that one here but it has been asked at least a hundred times! The answer is... I'll let you figure that one out. :)
------------------------------------------------------------
~ Q: What does this mod pack include? (SPOILERS, careful!)
A: 4 months in the making, this mod pack completely changes the look and feel of The Wind Waker.
Many things were changed, so here is the full list of content included in this mod pack.
------------------------------------------------------------

NOTE: If you encounter crashes of any kind, such as at the very beginning of the game, on Windfall or Dragon Roost Island, use GCFT to insert the files located in the "CRASH FIX" folder; kamome.arc and the ship.arc of your liking. This will fix any crash you have until I further optimize those files to not cause memory issues.

EDIT: I was also told of a crash during the Puppet Ganon fight, follow the same process to remove Zubat (Ki.arc) and maybe Ferroseed (Ks.arc) and replace them with the vanilla files since they take more memory.

Here is a project that was 5 months in the making, a mod that replaces MANY things in Wind Waker with Pokémon content. Play as Red (Randomizer-compatible), use various items and Pokémon from the series, and talk to / fight against many other Pokémon. View the video for more details!

The package is often updated when issues are fixed, especially memory-related ones. I also sometimes add more custom text and textures whenever I can so make sure to check the timer on the right for when the mod was last updated! If you encounter a crash, re-download the mod as I may have fixed it already. If not, please let me know of it!

profile._sText:
Changes Link to resemble Solid Snake from the Metal Gear series.

- Replaces Hero's Sword with a reverse grip combat knife.
- Turns the Hero's Shield invisible.
- Replaces bow and arrows with a USP, equipped with a Laser Aiming Module.
- Replaces bow and arrow sound effects with gunshot and ricochet sounds.
- Replaces the Master Sword with the Stun Knife.
- Replaces the Mirror Shield with a reflector.
- Replaces the Deku Leaf with a parachute.

Created using SuperBMD by Sage-of-Mirrors, and Wind Waker Model Helpers by LagoLunatic.

HOW TO INSTALL:

Requirements:
  • Dolphin Emulator.
  • A legally obtained Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker ISO.

Extracting your ISO:
This mod is easier to install with an extracted Wind Waker ISO. It makes editing individual files easier, and you won't have to worry about injecting files directly into the ISO.
  1. Open Dolphin, right click your Wind Waker ISO, and click on Properties. Go to the Filesystem tab.
  2. Right click on Disc, and click Extract All Files, and choose a new folder in an easily accessible location. (I.E. "C:\Users\John Doe\Documents\Dolphin Emulator\ISOs\LOZWW".)
  3. Extract the Apploader and DOL to the same folder.
  4. Click on Configure, and go to the Paths tab. Make sure your LOZWW folder is added to the ISO directories.
  5. Set your Default ISO as the boot.dol you just extracted.
  6. Set your DVD Root as the LOZWW folder.
  7. Set the Apploader to the apploader.img you extracted.
  8. Click OK.
  9. Without anything selected, click the Play button. This should launch the unpacked version of Wind Waker.

Installing the Model:
  1. In your extracted LOZWW folder, navigate to "res\Object".
  2. Create a backup of Link.arc.
  3. In "ATS_WWSNK", copy the Link.arc file to "LOZWW\res\Object".

Loading the Custom Textures: (OLD! NO LONGER REQUIRED FOR V2!)
  1. Navigate to "C:\Users\John Doe\Documents\Dolphin Emulator\Load\Textures". (You might have to create these folders if they don't exist.)
  2. Create a new folder in Textures called "00000000".
  3. Copy your custom textures from "ATS_WWSNK" to "00000000".
  4. Open Dolphin, and click on Graphics.
  5. In the Advanced tab, click on "Load Custom Textures".
  6. Click close, and now you're done! Your Wind Waker mod is now ready!

Here's a big fat skinpack for you all. The modelers gave their all to make these models, head over here to thank them if you got time: https://discord.gg/r2963mt

Created using SuperBMD by Sage-of-Mirrors, and Wind Waker Model Helpers by LagoLunatic.

Learn how to make a custom model with the help of this tutorial: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AuI9OHi6Ni2HUz...

Also keep in mind that these models were made in mind with the randomizer and weren't tested thoroughly in cutscenes, so oddities might show up from time to time.

HOW TO INSTALL:

Requirements:
  • Dolphin Emulator.
  • A legal copy of a Wind Waker ISO.

Extracting your ISO:
This mod is easier to install with an extracted Wind Waker ISO. It makes editing individual files easier, and you won't have to worry about injecting files directly into the ISO.
  1. Open Dolphin, right click your Wind Waker ISO, and click on Properties. Go to the Filesystem tab.
  2. Right click on Disc, and click Extract Entire Disc, and choose a new folder in an easily accessible location. (I.E. "C:\Users\John Doe\Documents\Dolphin Emulator\ISOs\LOZWW".)
  3. Click on Configure, and go to the Paths tab. Make sure your LOZWW folder is added to the ISO directories.
  4. Add the path for dolphin to find the boot.dol you just extracted.
  5. The game should appear in the game list, but with 0 bytes of data. This is normal. You can now open it like any other game.

Installing the Model:
  1. In your extracted models folder, open the folder of the model you would like to use.
  2. Create a backup of Link.arc located in "files\res\Object" of the extracted game files.
  3. Replace the vanilla Link.arc with the modded one.





Installing Custom Audio:
  1. Head over to "files\Audiores"
  2. Make a backup of jailnit.aaf
  3. From this current location, head to "\Banks" and make a backup of voice_0.aw
  4. Replace both files with the ones in the custom model folder.

profile._sText:
This is an HD texture pack for Twilight Princess. Based on familiar visuals, this pack faithfully recaptures the same HD look we've all grown accustomed to with thousands of enhancements, countless fixes and numerous carefully hand crafted custom textures. This texture pack covers the entire game, start to finish and every single texture's mipmap level was generated by eye every step of the way to ensure the best possible visual consistency throughout your playthrough. Get ready to experience this wonderful game once again in truly the most definitive way!

2.0 Features:

  • Over 1,100 newly improved textures and fixes
  • Highly optimized textures and better mipmap levels
  • Noticeably improved performance and stability
  • Numerous artstyle faithful HD custom textures
  • A start to finish bug-free playthrough experience
  • Significantly reduced clutter and better organization
  • New and improved Alternate Texture utilization system
  • ZeldArtist/Skilar Babcock's Alternate HD Link textures now included
  • Fully compatible with Dolphin, Dusklight and Courage Reborn
  • A refreshingly smaller overall filesize compared to 1.2.0
  • An optional performance friendly Reshade preset provided to achieve the same visuals in the showcase video and screenshots

Alternate Texture System Details

If you want to use this pack in combination with a different Button Layout, UI/HUD or any other texture replacements, you can very easily do so now within this version of TPDE+ itself. For example, if you want to use a different set of controller button textures for the UI, just open your TPDE+ folder and drop your custom button textures folder inside of "0 - Active Alt Textures" and you're done! Zero hassle and completely non-destructive. Anything placed in this folder will be loaded instead of the default equivalent as long as the filenames are identical. Feel free to customize your TPDE+ experience to your liking through this system!

How To Assemble Part 1, 2, 3, 4:

If you download this pack through the Alternate File Source, these assembly steps will not apply to you as that version is already fully assembled.

In order for this pack to be hosted directly on GameBanana, it must be split into 4 parts. GameBanana's filesize limit is 1.6GB for mods so this pack had to be divided for it to work. Yes, you DO need all 4 parts of this pack for the full and intended experience. It's quite simple to put these parts back together, so here's how to do it.

1.) Part 1 contains the main TPDE+ folder. Open your TPDE+ folder, then open the "2 - Environments & Objects" folder.

2.) Drag and drop the contents of Parts 2, 3 and 4 into the "2 - Environments & Objects" folder.

You're done. Click on "File Info" on any of these downloads to be taken to more in-depth installation instructions for Dolphin and Dusklight.

Yes, you'll sadly need 7-Zip to unpack these parts but the Alternate File Source version does not need 7-Zip.

- IMPORTANT INFO -

This page is now the official continuation of TPDE+. The Dusklight page for this texture pack is no longer able to be maintained by the previous page owner.

profile._sText:
Bem-vindos à tradução de The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess para Português de Portugal (PT-PT)!

Este projeto foi criado com o objetivo de trazer a aventura épica do Link no Reino do Crepúsculo para o nosso português, adaptando os diálogos, menus e itens de forma natural e rigorosamente fiel ao lore canónico da série Zelda.

? Nota sobre o Processo de Tradução:

Para acelerar o processo perante as milhares de linhas de texto do jogo, recorreu-se ao uso de Inteligência Artificial. Contudo, todo o texto passou por uma supervisão e revisão humana rigorosa para garantir que o contexto da história, o humor e as personalidades de cada personagem se mantivessem intactos e com a máxima qualidade no nosso idioma.

✨ Características

  • 100% PT-PT: Diálogos, interface de utilizador, tutoriais e descrições de itens adaptados para o português de Portugal.

  • Fidelidade ao Universo: Nomes de raças (os Zora, os Gorons), locais (Domínio dos Zora, Aldeia de Ordon) e itens clássicos (Espada Mestra, Pedaço de Coração) respeitam a nomenclatura oficial e consagrada.

  • Imersão total: Tratamento cerimonioso para figuras da realeza e espíritos, e expressões do dia a dia para as gentes das aldeias.

? Requisitos

  • Uma cópia/ISO limpa do The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess (versão GameCube). ⚠️ Atenção: É recomendado o uso da versão Americana (NTSC-U). A tradução foi desenvolvida com base nesta versão e não há garantia de que funcione corretamente numa ISO Europeia (PAL) ou Japonesa (NTSC-J).

  • O programa GameCube File Tools 2.0.0 (ou superior).

  • Um emulador (como o Dolphin) ou uma consola Wii/GameCube para jogar.

?️ Tutorial de Instalação

1.Preparar os Ficheiros:Extrai o ficheiro .zip da tradução que acabaste de descarregar. Vais obter uma pasta chamada Msgus.

2.Importar a ISO:Usando o GameCube File Tools.
  1. Abre o programa GameCube File Tools.

  2. No separador principal (GCM ISOs), clica no botão Import GCM.

  3. Seleciona a tua ISO original (limpa) Americana do Twilight Princess.

3.Substituir os ficheiros da pasta Msgus pela tradução :Aplicar a tradução diretamente na ISO.
  1. Na árvore de ficheiros do lado esquerdo, navega pelo seguinte caminho: expande files e depois expande res.

  2. Encontra a pasta chamada Msgus.

  3. Clica com o botão direito do rato em cima de Msgus e seleciona a opção Replace All Files in Folder.

  4. Na janela que abrir, seleciona a pasta Msgus que extraíste da minha tradução.

4.Exportar a ISO:Criar o novo jogo traduzido.
  1. Com os ficheiros já substituídos, clica no botão Export GCM (localizado no topo, por baixo de Import GCM).

  2. Escolhe onde queres guardar a tua nova ISO e dá-lhe um nome (por exemplo: Zelda_TP_PTPT.iso).

  3. Aguarda que o programa termine de exportar o jogo.

5.Jogar!:Carregar no emulador ou na consola.A tua nova ISO traduzida está pronta! Podes abri-la diretamente no emulador Dolphin ou passar o ficheiro para o teu cartão SD/Pen USB para jogares na consola original (usando o Nintendont, por exemplo). Boa aventura!

Coming from one of my first mods for SoH, I thought it fitting that my first mod for TP be replacing Link with Master Chief.

The mod replaces all of Link's models (Ordon Clothes, Hero's Clothes, Zora Armor, Magic Armor, and Sumo), as well as all of Link's Swords and Shields, and most of Link's voicelines being subbed out for Chief's voice. 

Wolf Link isn't included in this release as there are a few bugs to work out here and there with the game crashing, but look forward to Chief turning into a Mongoose sometime in the near future.

Installation (Dusklight):

  2. Finish the fight.


Installation (GC/Dolphin):
  1. Extract the files folder from the zip file somewhere you can find it easily.
  2. Open GCFT, and open your Twilight Princess ISO using the Import GCM option.
  3. Click Import Folder over GCM, and select the files folder from my mod.
  4. Click Export GCM, and rename it something other than Twilight Princess- I do not recommend overwriting your existing ISO file.
  5. Open your new ISO file in Dolphin, finish the fight.

For bug reporting feel free to comment issues below or hmu on Discord!

profile._sText:
English

The day has finally arrived! Everyone's favorite Cucco farmer has made her way to the Twilight Realm.

Special Thanks

I would like to thank ThenMichael and SimplySnaps for their support with ideas, testing, and design work.

A massive thank you goes to SkilarBabcock (ZeldaArtist on YT), who was instrumental in making this project a reality. Thank you for the tutoring, examples, help with modeling/texturing, and providing essential tools. Without them, this project might have remained just an idea.

This mod includes:

-Linkle Models: All 6 main outfits have been replaced (Ordon Clothes, Hero's Clothes, Zora Armor, Magic Armor, and Wolf Linkle).

-Voice Clips: All of Link’s voice lines have been replaced with Linkle’s voice (including clips from other characters voiced by the same Seiyu).

-Fixed Dialogues: English dialogues have been adjusted to use feminine pronouns. For the GameCube version.

-Custom Icons: Armor and dungeon map icons have been updated to match Linkle’s appearance.

-Cutscenes: Cutscene models have been fully replaced to ensure consistency.

Important Notes & Known Issues

-Model Limitations: Due to current tool limitations, two "HighPoly" face models remain unedited (the scene where Colin is kidnapped in Kakariko and the Lanayru Spring vision). Link’s original face will briefly appear during these moments.

Regarding the Wii Version: I have attempted to port the mod to the original Wii, but the audio consistently corrupts, resulting in a loud "crunchy" noise. For now, the Wii version is on hold. If a fix is found, I will release a dedicated update.

Español

¡Por fin ha llegado el día! Nuestra granjera de cucos favorita finalmente llega a las tierras del crepúsculo.

Agradecimientos Especiales

Antes que nada, quiero agradecer a ThenMichael y SimplySnaps por apoyarme con ideas, testeo y diseños.

Un agradecimiento enorme y especial a SkilarBabcock (ZeldaArtist en YT), quien fue el pilar fundamental de este proyecto. Gracias por las tutorías, los ejemplos, el apoyo en modelado y texturizado, y por las herramientas facilitadas. Sin su ayuda, este mod posiblemente se habría quedado solo en una idea.

¿Qué incluye este mod?

-Modelos de Linkle: he reemplazado los 6 modelos principales (Ropas de granja, Ropas del héroe, Armadura Zora, Armadura mágica y Link(le) Lobo).

-Clips de Voz: Todos los audios de Link han sido sustituidos por audios de Linkle (incluyendo algunos clips de otros personajes interpretados por su misma Seiyu para mayor variedad).

-Diálogos Localizados: He corregido los pronombres al femenino en Español. Además, para la versión de GameCube, he realizado un backport de los diálogos en Español Latino de la versión HD.

-Iconos Personalizados: Los iconos de armaduras y mapas de mazmorras han sido actualizados para reflejar el modelo de Linkle.

-Cinemáticas: Los modelos utilizados en las escenas de video también han sido reemplazados.

Notas Importantes y Errores Conocidos

-Limitación en los Modelos: Debido a las herramientas actuales, existen dos modelos "HighPoly" de la cara de Link que no se pueden reemplazar (en la escena del secuestro de Iván en Kakariko y en la visión de la Fuente de Lanayru). En esos momentos, aparecerá brevemente la cara original de Link.

-Revisión de Textos: Los diálogos en Inglés y Español España están verificados al 100%. El Español Latino debería estar perfecto también, pero al ser un proceso de conversión masivo, si encuentran algún error tipográfico, por favor repórtenlo enviando el texto completo y la parte del juego donde apareció.

¿Habrá versión de Wii? He intentado portear el mod a Wii, pero el audio se corrompe y produce un sonido "crujiente" y saturado cada que Linkle hace algo. Por ahora, la versión de Wii queda en estado indefinido. Si logro solucionarlo, publicaré una actualización dedicada.

Installation: 
Requirements: 
———————————————————————————————————————————————

-Your own  ISO of the game

-the GameCube FileTools (GCFT) utility. you can get it from: here

———————————————————————————————————————————————

1-Download & Extract: Download the mod and extract the .zip file (Desktop is recommended to avoid path errors). You will see a folder named "Linkle MOD (NTSC)".

2-Load ISO: Open GCFT, click the "Import GCM" button (top left), and select your ISO.

3-Replace Files: Click the "Add/Replace Files from folder" button (top right). Locate and select the Linkle mod folder.

4-Verification: A message should appear: "Importing files from this folder will replace 268 (This number may change in future updates) existing files and add 0 new files".

Important!: If the numbers are different or it says it’s adding new files, something is wrong. Make sure you selected the right folder. If it matches, click OK.

5-Export: Click the "Export GCM" button and choose where to save your new modded ISO.

Enjoy!: Run the ISO in Dolphin or move it to your modded console.

profile._sName: Twilight Princess Balanced HDR ReShade Preset
profile._sText:
I made this preset because most of the ones I found were either way too bright, way too dark, or just absolutely nuked the colours.

A lot of them (like the popular vibrance-style presets) tend to crush dark areas, blow out whites, and push everything way too yellow with over-the-top saturation and weird gamma. It ends up looking less like Twilight Princess and more like a filter slapped on top.

This is meant to sit in the middle. It keeps the original look of Twilight Princess, just cleaned up and brought closer to what you’d expect from a modern version.

(Tested primarily on the Wii version (RZDE01) via Dolphin.)

What this does

  • Adds some depth and contrast without crushing blacks
  • Brightens highlights without blowing everything out
  • Fixes that red/orange bleed you get with some presets
  • Gives colours a bit more life without turning everything neon
  • Slight ambient lift so darker areas aren’t a mess
It should feel like the same game, just sharper and clearer, not a completely different art style.

Important (recommended setup)

This preset was tuned while using the 4K texture pack, and it honestly looks best with it:

4K Texture Pack (Henriko):
https://www.henrikomagnifico.com/zelda-twilight-princess-4k

You can use this without it, but you won’t get the full effect.

ReShade install (quick guide)

If you don’t already have ReShade:

Download it here:
https://reshade.me/

Then:

  • Run the ReShade installer
  • Select your Dolphin.exe
  • Choose Vulkan when prompted
When asked for effects:

  • You can select the preset .ini file directly to install only the required shaders
  • Or just install the standard effects if you prefer
(Optional) You can enable addon support, but it’s not required for this preset

  • Launch Dolphin and start the game
  • Press Home to open ReShade
  • Select the preset

Dolphin settings I’m using

  • 4K (6x Native)
  • AA: Off
  • Anisotropic Filtering: 16x
  • Disable Copy Filter: On

Install – short version

  • Install ReShade into Dolphin
  • Drop the preset in
  • Select it in-game

Notes

  • Made for the normal Dolphin build, not Ishiruka
  • Works best at higher resolutions
  • Lighting will still vary depending on area/time of day (as intended)

Feedback

If anything looks off in certain areas, let me know.

Main things I’m interested in:

  • brightness balance
  • colours in different regions
  • night vs daytime

profile._sText:
The Master Sword in Twilight Princess is a noticeably brighter purple than its appearance in several other titles.

I have brought the brightness down a lot and added more blues back into its colour to try and make it resemble its appearance in BotW/TotK. In brighter light, it appears more blue/indigo, but at night its colour tends toward a more purple-ish hue.

It still has a really bright metallic sheen effect on  the handle which is presumably a property applied to those polygons, and is not related to the textures themselves, which is all this mod changes. So if you want the textures to look more matte, I cannot help there. But it's only really noticeable in dark spaces.


This is an edit of some of the textures of the Henriko Magnifico 4k texture packs, so I recommend installing those first, then dropping this GZ2 folder in the same location afterwards to overwrite the Master Sword textures.

I imagine the pack will work in isolation if you just drop these textures alone (albeit with a noticeably higher fidelity Master Sword than everything around it, but alas). Go to Dolphin, then open:

File > Open User Folder

then:

Load > Textures

Drop the GZ2 file in textures. Then make sure to enable custom textures in:

Dolphin > Options > Configuration > Graphics > Advanced

then check "Load Custom Textures" (optional "Prefetch Custom Textures" depending on performance).

profile._sText:
Includes three game modes:

  1. Rupee Damage
  2. Rupee Instakill
  3. Rupee Dash Mode

Rupee Damage: Link gets hurt when collecting a rupee.

Rupee Instakill: Link dies when collecting a rupee.

Rupee Dash Mode: an experimental remake of "Rupee Dash Mode" from Ship of Harkinian. Link loses a rupee every x second and he loses a heart if rupee is depleted.

If you already have a save file, make sure to backup your save file of the game before playing with this because it will likely overwrite your save file.

If you are playing wii version and on Dolphin emulator, after backing up your save, go to Tools -> Import Wii Save and select the bin file that is appropriate for your region. wus0.bin is for TP Wii USA 1.0 and wus2.bin is for TP Wii USA 1.2.

Regardless of whether you're playing on Wii or GC version of the game, after leaving the title screen and entering the file select screen, select the third file, then go through the title screen again, and then select the first or 2nd file and the mod should work!

Fixed a potential bug + added instaKill option -> Link dies as soon as he gets rupee.

15 February 2024 Update!

Added interactive terminal so no need to swap between two save files anymore. Added an experimental game mode: Rupee Dash Mode. The mod is now in Github instead of GameBanana. YouTube video made to showcase the mod.

25 February 2024 Update

profile._sText:
Twas the twilight before Christmas, and all through Hyrule,
everyone speaks endlessly of Christmas (even the mail fool).

If you're planning to re-play Twilight Princess this Christmas season, then this mod is for you!

COMPATIBLE WITH GAMECUBE (and probably USA version) ONLY

All of the text in the game has been madlibbed at random with words directly from all of the popular Christmas songs! Also the names of some people/places have been replaced by names of people/places from popular Christmas movies.

A few things to mention:
  • It is definitely not recommended to use this on your first play-through. Tutorials and important dialog meant to direct the player will be difficult to understand, so you'll want to already be familiar with the game.
  • Although funny, many sentences have grammar mistakes (computer no know Engrish). Not for grammar nazis. You've been warned.
  • In the game, people seem to speak about doves and pear trees to the point that it can get annoying. Maybe I should've excluded The Twelve Days of Christmas...
  • I also highly recommend  Adverse's Christmas Link mod.

How to use:

I have it set up to work really easy with the riivolution feature that recent Dolphin versions support. If using dolphin, export the files to ~/Documents/Dolphin Emulator/Load/Riivolution/ Then, right-click the game in Dolphin, choose to run it with riivolution, and open the .xml file in ~/Documents/Dolphin Emulator/Load/Riivolution/tp_christmas/riivolution/

You can also just inject the files into the iso instead if you prefer.

Merry Christmas

profile._sText:
This mod adds Blackjack to Wii Party Board Game Island! Once it's your turn to roll, you have the option to play a hand of blackjack instead of your normal dice roll by pressing 1. If you win, congrats! You will be awarded a Golden Die, which will roll a random number of spaces forward between 1 and 30. If you lose, oh no! You will be awarded a Flame Die, which will roll a random number of spaces backwards between 1 and 30. If you push, you will be awarded a die that will roll anywhere from positive 10 to negative 10 spaces. 

But there's more! Feeling lucky? You can choose to Double-Down during your turn. By pressing 2 before hitting, you will be dealt one additional card. If you win this hand, Lucky You! You will receive the Super Golden Die, this die will roll a positive number between 15 and 45. How advantageous! But if you lose a Double-Down... you won't be happy where you end up! Being dealt a natural Blackjack (21) on your turn will also result in you receiving the Super Golden Die!

If you have Gamble for Win enabled, once you or your opponents reach the top a hand of Blackjack will be dealt instead of the normal dice roll. If the hand is won, You Win! If the hand is lost, the player will be launched back 8 spaces from the top. Try again next time! If this hand results in a push, the player will remain at the top and can try again their next turn. 

There are 3 settings that control this mod
1.) Gamble for Roll - toggles optional Blackjack during player turns
2.) Gamble for Win - toggles Blackjack hand at the top instead of dice roll
3.) Card Back - choose between 9 unique card backs to be used during blackjack games 

Please let me know of any bugs/suggestions in the comments!

Compatibility: NTSC SUPE01, tested on Wii hardware. Dolphin compatibility currently untested. 

Credits:
Saulf - Custom dice assets
Alxala - Card sprites & backs

profile._sText:
This modpack uses Riivolution to allow you to selectively enable multiple mods at once. All mods have been edited by me to ensure compatibility, and some unreleased mods are even included as well. Works for NTSC-U and PAL, and should support every language.

If mods would be incompatible with each other, which is only the case for mods whose concepts directly conflict with each other, it is impossible to enable them both at the same time. Instead, you choose between them. Please note that I can offer limited support for mods that I did not personally create.

If you installed a previous version of the modpack and are trying to update, delete the wp-combined-mods folder from the root of your sd card, and follow the installation instructions, replacing files if prompted.

This mod uses Riivolution. There will be multiple pages on the GUI to enable all the options, make sure you look through them all!

Thanks to Haxyria, you can watch a video showcasing the mod here:


Previous videos:
v1.2

Mod List

Volatile Rolls by Saulf

The standard dice for winning are replaced with four news ones! Each dice has a separate probability for what number is actually rolled, and a second chance for if you move backwards. Probability of each number is not equal; lower/higher numbers are more unlikely (~20% for lowest 1/3 of numbers and ~20% for highest 1/3 of numbers) and middle numbers are the most likely (~60% for middle 1/3 of numbers.) First place can roll [0,30] and has a 29% chance of going backwards. Second place can roll [0,24] and has a 36% chance of going backwards. Third place can roll [0, 18] and has a 43% chance of going backwards. Last place can roll [0, 12] and has a 50% chance of going backwards.

Classic version: roll anywhere from -30 to +30! Luck becomes an even bigger factor in Wii Party as turns become more unpredictable. All numbers are equally likely.

Loser Moves Back by Saulf

Instead of receiving a single die, the loser of Board Game Island receives a set of double volcanic dice that move you backwards instead of forwards, safe for the volcano. Losing becomes even more punishing in this challenging twist.

Randomized Board Game Island by Dorian15, Saulf

The entire layout of Board Game Island is randomized! (Note: holding "2" while pressing start is no longer required for the mod to work. The board will always randomize when this mod is enabled.)

Addition by Saulf: I rewrote the code for better stability and introduced the blacklist from the Board Game Island spots editor tool to prevent crashes. I also added the customizable weights to change the odds of a space appearing and integrated the new custom spot.

"Back to Start" Space (Randomizer Option) by Chill Matt

A new space that will send you all the back to the start of the island! Features its own texture, and a unique purple spring when you are sent backwards.

Note from Saulf: This mod can only be played with the randomizer since there's no where to put it on the normal board. The original mod replaces the -4 space, but I updated it so that it is a new space instead, and added the purple spring.

Blind Board by  Haxyria, Packore, and Darce64

See how well you remember Board Game Island when all the spaces are a mystery; or play with the randomizer for an even more exciting twist! (Note: pressing - to show the map will no longer show any popup to avoid spoiling spaces.)

Randomized Globe Trot by Saulf, Dorian 15

Each spot on the globe is random, with the option to customize the weighted likelihood of each spot appearing. (Note: there is a minor visual bug when two adjacent spaces are the same type. In this case, there is no line connecting them, but the game functions as normal.)

Globe Trot lasts 20 rounds by Dorian15

Removes the bonus card from Globe Trot, making the game always reach the maximum of twenty rounds. 

Stomachache All Rounds by  LavAriz, Saulf

Choose from three different behaviors for the surprise spot in Globe Trot.
  1.  Equal Chance: All cards have an equal chance of appearing. This is not the default behavior of the game.  Usually, only certain cards can appear in certain rounds.
    2.  20% Stomachache: This makes Stomachache always have a 20% chance of appearing, but normal odds for the rest of the cards.
    3.  Always Stomachache: Stomachache will be the only card available on all surprise spots.

Extended Stopwatchers by Saulf

Makes the stopwatchers game generate a time anywhere from 10-55 instead of 5-10 seconds! See how well you can really keep track of time in this challenging variation.

Extended Walk-Off by Zen_364

This makes walk-off so that it can generate any distance from 0-999 yards/meters. The timer is set to 5 minutes, and the signs are placed further apart. (Note: There are some visual bugs during the final cutscene and when walking far distances.)

Wario in Shutterpup by Saulf, Vad

Instead of taking pictures of a dog, you can now take pictures of a Wario who's not afraid to bark. It doesn't change the gameplay, but it definitely adds some motivation.

New in update 1.3: Wario now wears 1 of 4 costumes at random! The costumes are: default Wario, Cowboy Wario, Thief/Purple Wind Wario, and Biker Wario. The costumes were made by Vad for Mario Sports Megamix.

Change P1,P2,P3,P4 Colors by Saulf

Adds the option to change the colors used for P1, P2, P3, and P4 separately. Some colors are kept, such as for certain items used in minigames where the colors are baked directly into the model, and other places like cursors. 

Play Against System Miis by Saulf, Boshi

With this mod enabled, whenever a CPU mii is randomly selected, it will instead randomly pick a Mii from your console that you have created (no guest Miis). Duplicate Miis are possible, especially if you have a small amount of Miis created.

Big Head Mode by Saulf

This makes all Miis have a huge head! It also makes Hide and Peek a bit easier depending on where you hide.

Change All Miis by Saulf

All Miis, including Miis on your system, will be replaced with one of four selectable Miis. This doesn't actually affect your save data nor your Wii Console. The four options are Beef Boss, Matt, Dudy Dude, and Grasshoper.

Rainbow Hair Color by Saulf

Choose a hair color to replace with an animated rainbow hair color!

Mr. (Ant) Tenna over Party Phil by citraDreamPainter

Replaces Party Phil with Mr. (Ant) Tenna, and includes voices!

Sebastian Tute over Party Phil by Saulf

Replaces Party Phil with Sebastian Tute!

Installation Instructions

The following can be used:

1. The latest version of Riivolution (Wii only)
2. The latest stable release of RiftWii (Wii/Wii U)
3. A recent version of Dolphin emulator

  1.  First, make sure you Wii/Wii U is modded.
  2.  Download the .zip file for this mod and extract it to the root of your SD card. The wp-combined-mods and riivolution folders should be on the root of your SD Card. When you double click the SD card in File Explorer to open it, the directory that opens is the root.
  3.  Launch Riivolution/alternative with the Wii Party disc inserted.
  4.  Choose which mods you want enabled. Certain mods are enabled by default. There are multiple pages that contain all of the mods.
  5.  Start the game!
If you are playing on dolphin, right click and then select "Start with Riivolution patches". Select the xml included in the downloaded which is in the riivolution folder.

Reporting Issues

If you have an issue, please leave a comment and specify:

  1.  Your game region
  2.  Your game language
  3.  Which mods were enabled
  4.  What steps you took to encounter this issue

profile._sText:
REQUEST

This mod was made first and foremost for LuigiTime202's request "Completing a classic": https://gamebanana.com/requests/97013
Thanks to them for the idea and for listing everything that was left unfinished in the game!

Wii Party has several minigame variants that were never used, their code and assets are still on the disc, but no game mode can launch them. This mod restores all of them without removing anything from the base game.

WHAT'S ADDED

Pop-Up Bandits, 4-player free-for-all
- The unused 4-player version of the 1 vs 1 shooting game.
- Shows up in Free Play (4-Player list) and in the random minigame draws of the party modes, like any other 4-player minigame.

Barrel Daredevil, 1 vs 1
- The unused duel version of the 4-player game.
- Shows up in Free Play (1 vs 1 list) and in the random 1 vs 1 draws (e.g. Board Game Island duels).

Spot the Sneak / Rule Reversal: 5 unused minigames
- Derby Dash
- Shifty Gifts
- Quicker Chipper
- Tropical Punch
- Ball Brawl (Crash Balls in the NA version)
All five contain the complete cheater code (secret advantage, "cheating practice", press B to stop cheating). They are now part of the Rule Reversal pool, alongside the 12 original games. As in the original game, they are only played in that mode.

FIXES TO LEFTOVERS
- The cheater's secret rule of the 5 Rule Reversal games was never translated (Japanese only, in every language). It is now written in English, French, German, Italian, Spanish and Dutch.
- The two new variants had Japanese placeholder names and rules. They now use their proper names and rules in every language.
- Free Play thumbnails, rules screen, controls screen and preview movie are set up for the new variants, so no "DUMMY" picture or empty screen.
- When 2 or more CPUs play Rule Reversal, the game uses a shorter list of minigames where the cheat is visible on screen. Shifty Gifts, Quicker Chipper, Tropical Punch and Ball Brawl were added to it too. Derby Dash is left out, because the game removes a CPU cheater's advantage in that minigame.

REQUIREMENTS
- Wii Party, European (PAL, SUPP01) or North American (NTSC-U, SUPE01) version. Download the matching file. Other regions are not supported.
- Riivolution (Wii) or Dolphin.

INSTALLATION

Wii (Homebrew Channel + Riivolution)
1. Copy the content of the archive to the root of your SD card (the "riivolution" and "UnusedMinigames" folders must be at the root).
2. Launch Riivolution with the Wii Party disc inserted.
3. Set "Unused Minigames" to "Enabled", then "Launch".

Dolphin
1. Copy the content of the archive to Dolphin's Load/Riivolution folder.
2. Right-click Wii Party > "Start with Riivolution Patches".
3. Enable "Unused Minigames", then "Start".

NOTES
- Rule Reversal must be unlocked in your save as usual.
- The new variants share the "played" checkmark and unlock status of their used counterparts (Barrel Daredevil 4P / Pop-Up Bandits 1 vs 1), so your save data stays untouched and compatible.
- The rules screen background and preview movie of the two new variants are the ones of their counterpart. For exl shows the 4-player preview.
- Tested in Dolphin (Free Play and full Rule Reversal games). Not yet tested on a real Wii: feedback welcome!

Made for the "Completing a classic" request.

profile._sName: Board Game Island: The Floor Is Lava
profile._sText:
The Floor Is Lava turns Board Game Island into a race against a rising sea of lava.

How it plays
- The island is surrounded by lava, under the volcano's eruption sky, for the whole game.
- At the end of every round, the lava rises. It follows the real height of the island and swallows about 8% of the board each round, a whole plateau at once when it reaches one.
- Any player standing on a space under the lava gets burnt and falls into the volcano. When they get out of the volcano, they land 5 spaces ahead of the lava.
- If the lava swallows the final challenge before anyone has passed it, the game is over and nobody wins. That happens by round 14 at the latest, so don't wait at the gate too long!
- The minimap shows the part of the route already under the lava in orange.
- Everything else is the original game: minigames, bonus dice, special spaces, the volcano, the final challenge.

Features
- A real 3D lava sheet over the whole map, with the volcano's own animated lava.
- The volcano eruption ambiance all the time (red sky, smoke, ash, fog).
- A cutscene when the lava rises, and another one when a player gets caught.
- A warning when the lava gets close to the final challenge.
- New messages in all 6 European languages: English, French, German, Italian, Spanish and Dutch.

Requirements
- Wii Party, European version (PAL, SUPP01). Other regions are not supported.
- Riivolution on a Wii (Homebrew Channel), or Dolphin with Riivolution support.

Installation (Wii)
1. Extract the archive to the root of your SD card (the riivolution and LavaMode folders must be at the root).
2. Launch Riivolution and insert your Wii Party disc.
3. Set Lava Mode to Enabled, then press Launch.
4. Play Board Game Island as usual.

Installation (Dolphin)
Right-click Wii Party in the game list -> Start with Riivolution Patches…, choose the folder that contains the extracted riivolution and LavaMode folders, enable Lava Mode, then Start.

Notes
- This mod replaces Board Game Island's code (mr001.rel). It cannot be combined with other mods that also change Board Game Island.
- Crashes are possible. If the game crashes, please report it in the comments below.
- All suggestions are welcome! Ideas, balance changes, new features. Tell me in the comments.

Credits
Built from the Wii Party decompilation project (InputEvelution/wp).

profile._sText:
Duo Mode turns Board Game Island into a team race: Player 1 + Player 3 (blue) against Player 2 + Player 4 (red).

How to win: roll 6 or higher at the final gate to pass the challenge. The first member of a team waits at the gate, cheering. When the teammate passes too, both break the wall together, climb the stairs side by side and celebrate as a team.

Team rules:
 - The Tornado never targets your own teammate; the UFO can swap you with your teammate.
 - Players who already passed the final challenge are out of reach: no Tornado, no UFO, no duel.
 - When only 2 players are still racing, the round minigame becomes a 1 vs 1 between them.
 - 1 vs 3 spaces become 1 vs 1 when fewer than 3 opponents are still racing.

New space: Team Swap. P1 switches places with P2, and P3 with P4 (2 on the board).

Team colours everywhere: team jerseys, order-of-play HUD, player panels, turn banner, minimap, player name panels. The "Left:" panel shows the team's total. Host messages are rewritten in all 6 PAL languages.

Requirements: Wii Party PAL (SUPP01), plus Riivolution on Wii or Dolphin. Start a new Board Game Island game with the mod enabled.

Installation: see README.txt in the archive. Wii: copy to the SD root, then Riivolution → Enable "Duo Mode". Dolphin: copy to Load/Riivolution, then right-click the game → Start with Riivolution Patches.
